paras.en: [[10:3|But when|Ab hac sapientia, ut]], that is, after, [[10:3|the unjust went away from her|recessit injustus]], from this wisdom, namely Cain, who after his fall did not repent but despaired, saying: [[Gen 4:13|My iniquity is greater|Major est]], he says, [[Gen 4:13|than that I may deserve pardon|iniquitas mea, quam ut veniam merear]]; [[10:3|in his anger|in ira sua]], that is, through the wrath which he conceived against just Abel, whom he also envied; [[10:3|by the fury wherewith he murdered|per iram homicidii]], that is, through his vicious wrath, out of which he committed fratricide by slaying Abel himself[[Gen 4:8||]], [[10:3|he perished|fraternitas deperiit]] [Denis reads *fraternitas deperiit*, "brotherhood perished", where the Vulgate has *fraterni deperiit*, "he perished by the fury of the murder of his brother"], that is, his brother was killed, and brotherly love too was destroyed on his part.

paras.t: Propter quod, id est propter sapientiæ derelictionem, seu propter recessum a Sapientia increata, et a sapientiæ dono, quum aqua deleret terram, id est, diluvium submergeret genus humanum. Vel : Propter hoc, id est propter scelus Cain, quum aqua diluvii deleret totam ipsius Cain posteritatem, quæ patris sui malignitatem fuit secuta. Sicque in diluvio fuit soluta vindicta piaculi tanti, secundum Glossam : quæ tamen et in ipso Cain cœpit antea exerceri. Sanavit iterum sapientia, id est, genus humanum reparavit, per contemptibile lignum, id est per arcam factam de lignis, justum gubernans, id est, ipsum Noe cum sobole sua conservans, et per filios ejus genus humanum multiplicans, ut patet in Genesi.
paras.en: [[10:4|For whose cause|Propter quod]] [Denis reads *propter quod*, "for which cause"], that is, because wisdom was forsaken, or because of the going away from the uncreated Wisdom and from the gift of wisdom, [[10:4|when water destroyed the earth|quum aqua deleret terram]], that is, when the flood drowned the human race[[Gen 7:17||]] [the margin gives Gen. vii, 17–23]. Or: For this cause, that is, because of the crime of Cain, when the water of the flood destroyed the whole posterity of Cain himself, which had followed the malice of its father. And so in the flood the vengeance for so great a crime was paid, according to the Gloss: a vengeance which had nevertheless begun to be exacted earlier on Cain himself[[Gen 4:11||]][[Gen 4:12||]]. [[10:4|wisdom healed it again|Sanavit iterum sapientia]], that is, restored the human race, [[10:4|by contemptible wood|per contemptibile lignum]], that is, by the ark made of timber[[Gen 6:14||]], [[10:4|directing the course of the just|justum gubernans]], that is, preserving Noe himself with his offspring, and multiplying the human race through his sons, as is clear in Genesis[[Gen 6:1||]] [the margin gives Gen. vi–x, the whole story of Noe].

paras.t: Hæc et in consensu superbiæ, quum se nationes extulissent, scivit justum : id est, sapientia conservavit et approbavit ipsum Abraham virtuosum, postquam perversæ nationes natæ ex semine filiorum Noe extulerunt se, concorditer superbientes et superbe consentientes ad ædificandum turrim Babel, dicentes : Venite, faciamus nobis civitatem et turrim, cujus cacumen pertingat ad cœlum; et celebremus nomen nostrum antequam dividamur in universas terras. Quod etiam facere voluerunt, ut ad turrim illam confugerent, si de cetero diluvium inundaret. Et conservavit sine querela Deo, id est, ipsum Abraham ad laudem Dei præservavit a vitiis, et irreprehensibiliter vivere fecit. Cui dixit : Ambula coram me, et esto perfectus; et, Ego protector tuus, et merces tua magna nimis. Et in filiis misericordiam fortem custodivit, id est, posteris Abrahæ, scilicet ipsis Isaac et Jacob, et eorum posteritati stabilem exhibuit pietatem, prout legitur in Deuteronomio : En Domini Dei tui cœlum est, et cœli cœlorum, terra et omnia quæ in eis sunt; et tamen patribus tuis conglutinatus est Dominus, et elegit eos, amavitque semen eorum post eos.
paras.en: [[10:5|Moreover, when the nations had conspired together to consent to wickedness, she knew the just|Hæc et in consensu superbiæ, quum se nationes extulissent, scivit justum]] [Denis reads *in consensu superbiæ, quum se nationes extulissent*, "in the consent of pride, when the nations had lifted themselves up", where the Vulgate has *nequitiæ* and *contulissent*]: that is, wisdom preserved and approved the virtuous Abraham himself, after the perverse nations born of the seed of Noe's sons had lifted themselves up, proud in concord and consenting in pride to build the tower of Babel, saying: [[Gen 11:4|Come, let us make a city and a tower, the top whereof may reach to heaven; and let us make our name famous before we be scattered abroad into all lands|Venite, faciamus nobis civitatem et turrim, cujus cacumen pertingat ad cœlum; et celebremus nomen nostrum antequam dividamur in universas terras]]. This too they meant to do so that they might take refuge in that tower if a flood should overflow again. [[10:5|and preserved him without blame to God|Et conservavit sine querela Deo]], that is, kept Abraham himself from vices, to the praise of God, and made him live blamelessly. To him he said: [[Gen 17:1|walk before me, and be perfect|Ambula coram me, et esto perfectus]]; and, [[Gen 15:1|I am thy protector, and thy reward exceeding great|Ego protector tuus, et merces tua magna nimis]]. And in his sons she kept a strong mercy [Denis reads *in filiis misericordiam fortem custodivit*, where the Vulgate has *in filii misericordia fortem custodivit*, which the Douay-Rheims renders "and kept him strong against the compassion for his son"], that is, she showed a steadfast loving-kindness to the descendants of Abraham, namely to Isaac and Jacob themselves and to their posterity, as we read in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 10:14|Behold heaven is the Lord's thy God, and the heaven of heaven, the earth and all things that are therein|En Domini Dei tui cœlum est, et cœli cœlorum, terra et omnia quæ in eis sunt]]; [[Deut 10:15|And yet the Lord hath been closely joined to thy fathers, and loved them and chose their seed after them|et tamen patribus tuis conglutinatus est Dominus, et elegit eos, amavitque semen eorum post eos]] [Denis has *elegit eos, amavitque semen eorum*, "chose them, and loved their seed"].

paras.t: Hæc sapientia justum Lot a pereuntibus impiis, scilicet Sodomitis, liberavit fugientem cum uxore sua, duabusque filiabus, angelis eum educentibus, descendente igne sulfureo in Pentapolim, id est quinque urbes vitio contra naturam laborantes : quarum quatuor in Deuteronomio exprimuntur, quum dicitur : Sodoma, Gomorrha, Adama, Seboim.
paras.en: [[10:6|She delivered the just man|Hæc sapientia justum]] Lot, [[10:6|who fled from the wicked that were perishing|a pereuntibus impiis, scilicet Sodomitis, liberavit fugientem]], namely the Sodomites, as he fled with his wife and his two daughters, the angels leading him out[[Gen 19:16||]][[Gen 19:17||]], [[10:6|when the fire came down upon Pentapolis|descendente igne sulfureo in Pentapolim]] [Denis adds *sulfureo*, "of brimstone"], that is, upon the five cities labouring under the vice against nature, four of which are named in Deuteronomy, where it says: [[Deut 29:23|Sodom and Gomorrha, Adama and Seboim|Sodoma, Gomorrha, Adama, Seboim]].

paras.t: Quibus Sodomitis, id est ad perpetuam eorum confusionem atque diffamiam, in testimonium, scilicet nequitiæ eorumdem, fumigabunda constat terra deserta : id est, terra regionis eorum manet inhabitabilis, et [surgit] fumus fœtidus teterrimusque in signum fœtoris turpissimique ardoris carnalitatis eorum ; et incerto tempore fructus habentes arbores, id est, in testimonium turpitudinis Sodomitarum, stant ibi arbores, quæ fructus pulchros habere videntur tempore incerto, id est innaturali atque insolito, sicut et illi contra naturam peccaverunt : qui fructus dum manu tanguntur, in cinerem redigi perhibentur, ad ostendendum quod animæ impiorum illorum sine fructu pœnitentiæ emigrantes, in inferno perpetuæ ardent; et incredibilis animæ memoria, id est, memoriale incredulæ animæ uxoris Lot est ibi, stans figmentum salis, id est species seu statua salis, in quam corpus illius conversum est, ob suam incredulitatem et inobedientiam : quoniam contra Dei præceptum retrospexit, prout ista historia in Genesi plenius continetur. Cujus et sacratissimus princeps Apostolorum in sua secunda Canonica meminit, dicens : Civitates Sodomorum et Gomorrhæorum in cinerem Dominus redigens, eversione damnavit, exemplum eorum qui impie acturi sunt, ponens; et justum Lot oppressum, a nefandorum injuria ac luxuriosa conversatione eripuit. Unde uxor Lot in salem conversa, usque in præsens nos sallit, dum ejus exemplo ab incredulitatis et inobedientiæ vitiis abstinemus. Propter quod in Evangelio monet Salvator : Memores estote uxoris Lot. Refert Josephus se statuam illam vidisse.
paras.en: [[10:7|Whose|Quibus]] (that is, the Sodomites', to their perpetual confusion and ill fame) land, [[10:7|for a testimony|in testimonium]], namely of their wickedness, [[10:7|is desolate, and smoketh to this day|fumigabunda constat terra deserta]]: that is, the land of their region remains uninhabitable, and a fetid and most foul smoke rises from it, as a sign of the stench and of the most shameful burning of their carnality; [[10:7|and the trees bear fruits that ripen not|et incerto tempore fructus habentes arbores]] [literally "trees having fruit at an uncertain time"], that is, as a testimony to the filthiness of the Sodomites, there stand there trees which seem to bear fair fruit at an uncertain time, that is, an unnatural and unwonted one, just as those men sinned against nature; and these fruits, when touched by the hand, are said to fall into ashes, to show that the souls of those wicked men, departing without the fruit of penance, burn for ever in hell; and [[10:7|a monument of an incredulous soul|et incredibilis animæ memoria]], that is, the memorial of the incredulous soul of Lot's wife is there, [[10:7|a standing pillar of salt|stans figmentum salis]], that is, the likeness or statue of salt into which her body was turned[[Gen 19:26||]] for her incredulity and disobedience, since she looked back against God's command[[Gen 19:17||]], as this story is told more fully in Genesis. The most holy prince of the Apostles also makes mention of it in his second Canonical Epistle, saying: [[2 Pet 2:6|reducing the cities of the Sodomites and of the Gomorrhites into ashes, condemned them to be overthrown, making them an example to those that should after act wickedly|Civitates Sodomorum et Gomorrhæorum in cinerem Dominus redigens, eversione damnavit, exemplum eorum qui impie acturi sunt, ponens]]; [[2 Pet 2:7|And delivered just Lot, oppressed by the injustice and lewd conversation of the wicked|et justum Lot oppressum, a nefandorum injuria ac luxuriosa conversatione eripuit]]. Hence Lot's wife, turned into salt, salts us even to this day [Denis plays on *salem*, "salt", and *sallit*, "salts", that is, seasons us with wisdom], while by her example we keep from the vices of incredulity and disobedience. For this reason the Saviour warns in the Gospel: [[Luke 17:32|Remember Lot's wife|Memores estote uxoris Lot]]. Josephus relates that he saw that statue.

paras.t: Porro Magister in Historiis scribit : Versa est regio illa Pentapolis in lacum salsum ac sterilem : qui dicitur mare Mortuum, quia nec pisces, nec aves in eo vivere possunt. Navem non patitur, nec aliquam materiam aliam, nisi bituminatam. Poma nata in arboribus circumpositis, usque ad maturitatem viridis sunt coloris : quæ dum matura inciduntur, favillam intus habere inveniuntur. Atque, ut Josephus recitat, præ nimia levitate materiæ laci illius, etiam gravissima in eam projecta ascendunt. Nam et Vespasianus quosdam, vinctis post tergum manibus, projici fecit in profundum ipsius : qui omnes quasi vi venti sursum impulsi, desuper fluitabant.
paras.en: Moreover the Master writes in the Histories [that is, Peter Comestor, in the *Historia scholastica*]: That region of the Pentapolis was turned into a salt and barren lake, which is called the Dead Sea, because neither fish nor birds can live in it. It does not bear a ship, nor any other material unless it is coated with bitumen. The apples that grow on the trees round about are green in colour until they are ripe; and when they are cut open ripe, they are found to have ashes inside. And, as Josephus recounts [the margin gives *De Bello Judaico* iv, 27], because of the exceeding lightness of the matter of that lake, even the heaviest things thrown into it come up. For Vespasian, too, had certain men thrown into its depths with their hands bound behind their backs: and all of them, driven upwards as though by the force of the wind, floated on the top.

paras.t: Sapientiam enim prætermittentes, id est relinquentes, non tantum in hoc inconveniens lapsi sunt, ut ignorarent bona cœlestia, ac spiritualia ac divina, veramque felicitatem, et opera bona virtutum, per quæ ad illam pertingitur : quæ omnia per sapientiam cognoscuntur ; sed et insipientiæ suæ reliquerunt hominibus memoriam. Quemadmodum enim quidam bene feliciterque famosi sunt, propter excellentiam suæ sapientiæ ac virtutum ; sic quidam male infeliciterque sunt famosi, propter excessum suæ insipientiæ ac impietatum. Quod ad incrementum calamitatis eorum, et ad augmentum damnationis ipsorum vergit et confert : quoniam in inferno participes fiunt pœnarum illorum, qui exemplis ipsorum ad vitia incitantur ac animantur. Ut in his quæ peccaverunt, id est in vitiosis actibus suis, nec latere potuissent : quia in publicum deducuntur, et frequenter per pœnas a Deo inflictas, eorum manifestantur peccata. Quod tamen Omnipotens facit ad electorum suorum profectum atque cautelam : quatenus exemplo confusionis punitionisque reproborum, a vitiis abstrahantur. Etenim pestilente flagellato, stultus sapientior erit.
paras.en: [[10:8|For regarding not wisdom|Sapientiam enim prætermittentes]], that is, forsaking it, [[10:8|they did not only slip in this|non tantum in hoc inconveniens lapsi sunt]] unseemly fault, [[10:8|that they were ignorant of good things|ut ignorarent bona]], heavenly, spiritual and divine, and of true happiness, and of the good works of the virtues by which it is reached, all of which are known through wisdom; [[10:8|but they left also unto men a memorial of their folly|sed et insipientiæ suæ reliquerunt hominibus memoriam]]. For just as some are famous for good and happily, because of the excellence of their wisdom and virtues, so some are famous for ill and unhappily, because of the excess of their folly and impieties. And this tends and contributes to the increase of their calamity and the growth of their damnation, since in hell they come to share in the punishments of those who are spurred on and encouraged to vice by their examples. [[10:8|so that in the things in which they sinned|Ut in his quæ peccaverunt]], that is, in their vicious acts, [[10:8|they could not so much as lie hid|nec latere potuissent]]: for they are brought out in public, and their sins are often made manifest through the punishments that God inflicts. Yet the Almighty does this for the profit and the warning of his elect, so that by the example of the confusion and punishment of the reprobate they may be drawn away from vices. For [[Prov 19:25|The wicked man being scourged, the fool shall be wiser|pestilente flagellato, stultus sapientior erit]].

paras.t: Sapientia autem hos qui se observant, id est, diligenter custodiunt, et per obedientiam intra se retinent, a doloribus liberabit. Nam eripit a peccatis, et a tormentis quæ infliguntur pro illis. Confert etiam mentis tranquillitatem, et ad pacem perducit æternitatis. Et quamvis electi in præsenti vita bonis et salubribus afficiantur doloribus, pro suis et proximorum peccatis, et ex desiderio futuræ beatitudinis, ex meditatione quoque dominicæ passionis; tamen de omnibus his transferuntur ad gloriam tanto majorem, quanto hic amplius tam salubriter affliguntur. Ideo scriptum est : Multæ tribulationes justorum, et de his omnibus liberabit eos Dominus.
paras.en: [[10:9|But wisdom|Sapientia autem]] [[10:9|hath delivered from sorrow|a doloribus liberabit]] [Denis reads *liberabit*, "will deliver"] [[10:9|them that attend upon her|hos qui se observant]], that is, who keep her diligently and hold her within themselves by obedience. For she rescues them from sins and from the torments that are inflicted for them. She also bestows tranquillity of mind, and leads them to the peace of eternity. And although the elect in this present life are touched with good and wholesome sorrows, for their own sins and their neighbours', and out of longing for the beatitude to come, and also from meditating on the Lord's passion, yet out of all these they are carried over to a glory so much the greater as they are here the more afflicted, and so wholesomely. Therefore it is written: [[Ps 33:20|Many are the afflictions of the just; but out of them all will the Lord deliver them|Multæ tribulationes justorum, et de his omnibus liberabit eos Dominus]].

paras.t: Hæc autem sapientia profugum iræ fratris justum, id est Sapientia increata ipsum Jacob patriarcham virtuosum, ab ira fratris sui Esau fugientem in Mesopotamiam, ut patet in Genesi, deduxit per vias rectas, id est per semitas æquitatis, ita quod in fuga illa non est motus invidia contra fratrem, nec per impatientiam vitiatus, sed virtutibus mansit inhærens. Per vias quoque materiales rectas ipsum perduxit, sicut et Eliezer servus Abrahæ dixit : Benedictus Dominus, qui recto itinere me perduxit in domum fratris domini mei Abrahæ. Et ostendit illi regnum Dei, id est gloriam electorum, et præmia virtuosorum manifestavit ei in visione in somno, quando vidit imaginaria visione scalam in terra stantem usque ad cœlum pertingere, et Dominum in cacumen scalæ procumbentem, sibi mox dicere : Ego sum Deus Abraham patris tui : terram in qua dormis, tibi dabo et semini tuo, et benedicentur in te et in semine tuo cunctæ tribus terræ. Quæ utique promissio, de Christo exponitur. Unde, quod tunc de cœlesti patria et de ingressu in eam, revelationem habuerit, constat ex eo, quod tunc ad se reversus, protinus dixit : Quam terribilis est locus iste! Non est hic aliud, nisi domus Dei et porta cœli. Et dedit illi scientiam sanctorum, id est salutarem scientiam divinorum : quæ datur Sanctis, et est donum Spiritus Sancti, quod tunc auctum fuit in eo. Dedit quoque ei tunc scientiam sanctorum, id est notitiam solito ampliorem angelorum beatorum, quos in scala vidit ascendentes ac descendentes.
paras.en: [[10:10|She conducted the just, when he fled from his brother's wrath|Hæc autem sapientia profugum iræ fratris justum]], that is, the uncreated Wisdom conducted the virtuous patriarch Jacob himself as he fled from the wrath of his brother Esau[[Gen 27:41||]] into Mesopotamia[[Gen 28:5||]], as is clear in Genesis, [[10:10|through the right ways|deduxit per vias rectas]], that is, along the paths of equity, so that in that flight he was not moved by envy against his brother, nor tainted by impatience, but remained cleaving to the virtues. She also led him along right ways in the bodily sense, as Eliezer, Abraham's servant, also said: [[Gen 24:27|Blessed be the Lord|Benedictus Dominus]], who [[Gen 24:27|hath brought me the straight way into the house of my master's brother|qui recto itinere me perduxit in domum fratris domini mei Abrahæ]]. [[10:10|and shewed him the kingdom of God|Et ostendit illi regnum Dei]], that is, made manifest to him the glory of the elect and the rewards of the virtuous in a vision in his sleep, when in an imaginary vision [that is, a vision of images formed in the imagination, as distinct from bodily and intellectual vision] he saw a ladder standing on the earth and reaching up to heaven[[Gen 28:12||]], and the Lord leaning on the top of the ladder, who presently said to him: [[Gen 28:13|I am the Lord God of Abraham thy father|Ego sum Deus Abraham patris tui]]: [[Gen 28:13|The land, wherein thou sleepest, I will give to thee and to thy seed|terram in qua dormis, tibi dabo et semini tuo]], [[Gen 28:14|and IN THEE and thy seed, all the tribes of the earth SHALL BE BLESSED|et benedicentur in te et in semine tuo cunctæ tribus terræ]]. And this promise is certainly explained of Christ. Hence that he then had a revelation of the heavenly fatherland and of the entry into it is plain from this, that on coming to himself he said at once: [[Gen 28:17|How terrible is this place? this is no other but the house of God, and the gate of heaven|Quam terribilis est locus iste! Non est hic aliud, nisi domus Dei et porta cœli]]. [[10:10|and gave him the knowledge of the holy things|Et dedit illi scientiam sanctorum]] [*sanctorum* may mean "of holy things" or "of the holy ones"; Denis takes it both ways], that is, the saving knowledge of divine things, which is given to the Saints and is a gift of the Holy Ghost, which was then increased in him. She also gave him then the knowledge of the holy ones, that is, a fuller knowledge than usual of the blessed angels, whom he saw ascending and descending on the ladder[[Gen 28:12||]].

paras.t: Honestavit illum in laboribus suis, id est, ostendit quod ipse Jacob juste se habuit, pascendo et custodiendo pecora Laban valde laboriose. Propter quod ait : Die noctuque urebar æstu et gelu, fugiebat somnus ab oculis meis; sic per viginti annos servivi tibi. Et complevit labores illius, dando ei perseverantiam ac mercedem. In fraude circumvenientium illum adfuit, id est, sapientia pie adstitit ipsi Jacob in deceptionibus, quibus Laban et filii ejus nitebantur ipsum Jacob decipere, frequenter mutando ejus mercedem, secundum quod Jacob : Immutasti, inquit, mercedem meam decem vicibus. Et honestum fecit illum, id est, virtuosum, et cum grandi opulentia reduxit eum ad propria, ejusque probitatem in omnibus demonstravit.
paras.en: [[10:10|made him honourable in his labours|Honestavit illum in laboribus suis]], that is, she showed that Jacob himself behaved justly, feeding and keeping the flocks of Laban with very great labour. Therefore he says: [[Gen 31:40|Day and night was I parched with heat, and with frost, and sleep departed from my eyes|Die noctuque urebar æstu et gelu, fugiebat somnus ab oculis meis]]; [[Gen 31:41|in this manner have I served thee|sic per viginti annos servivi tibi]] twenty years. [[10:10|and accomplished his labours|Et complevit labores illius]], by giving him perseverance and a reward. [[10:11|In the deceit of them that overreached him, she stood by him|In fraude circumvenientium illum adfuit]], that is, wisdom lovingly stood by Jacob himself in the deceptions by which Laban and his sons strove to deceive Jacob himself, often changing his wages, according to what Jacob says: [[Gen 31:41|thou hast changed|Immutasti]], he says, [[Gen 31:41|my wages ten times|mercedem meam decem vicibus]]. [[10:11|and made him honourable|Et honestum fecit illum]], that is, virtuous; and she brought him back home with great wealth[[Gen 32:5||]][[Gen 32:10||]], and showed his uprightness in all things.

paras.t: Custodivit illum ab inimicis suis, scilicet a Laban et fratribus ejus, qui insequebantur eum animo persequendi ac spoliandi. Unde dixit ad Laban : Nisi Deus patris mei Abraham adfuisset mihi, forsitan modo me nudum dimisisses. Et a seductoribus tutavit, id est, securum fecit, illum. Nam dixit ad Laban : Cave ne quidquam aspere loquaris contra Jacob.
paras.en: [[10:12|She kept him safe from his enemies|Custodivit illum ab inimicis suis]], namely from Laban and his brethren, who were following him with the intention of persecuting and despoiling him[[Gen 31:23||]]. Hence he said to Laban: [[Gen 31:42|Unless the God of my father, Abraham|Nisi Deus patris mei Abraham]], [[Gen 31:42|had stood by me, peradventure now thou hadst sent me away naked|adfuisset mihi, forsitan modo me nudum dimisisses]]. [[10:12|and she defended him from seducers|Et a seductoribus tutavit]], that is, made him safe. For God said to Laban: [[Gen 31:24|Take heed thou speak not any thing harshly against Jacob|Cave ne quidquam aspere loquaris contra Jacob]].

paras.t: Et certamen forte dedit illi, videlicet luctam cum angelo, ut vinceret vel angelum sanctum, non fortitudine, sed devotione, id est, per modum vincentis haberet se, quadam quasi importunitate extorquendo ab angelo benedictionem. Quum enim dixisset angelus, Dimitte me, jam enim ascendit aurora; respondit : Non dimittam te, nisi benedixeris mihi. Vel, Ut vinceret adversarios suos, homines sibi inimicantes : et præsertim, ut invisibiles suæ salutis vinceret inimicos. Hinc angelus dixit ei : Si contra Deum fortis fuisti, quanto magis contra homines prævalebis? In Genesi quoque Jacob ait ad Joseph : Do tibi partem unam extra fratres tuos, quam […]tudine sua directus est cum angelo : et invaluit ad angelum, et confortatus est; flevit, et rogavit eum. Et sciret, id est, in se ipso per auxilia sibi divinitus exhibita experiretur, atque ex divina illuminatione ampliori clarius cognosceret, quoniam omnium potentior est sapientia increata, quæ vere omnipotens est, et suis cultoribus victoriam ad libitum tribuens.
paras.en: [[10:12|and gave him a strong conflict|Et certamen forte dedit illi]], namely the wrestling with the angel[[Gen 32:24||]], [[10:12|that he might overcome|ut vinceret]] even the holy angel, not by strength but by devotion: that is, that he might bear himself after the manner of one who overcomes, wresting the blessing from the angel by a kind of importunity. For when the angel had said, [[Gen 32:26|Let me go, for it is break of day|Dimitte me, jam enim ascendit aurora]], he answered: [[Gen 32:26|I will not let thee go, except thou bless me|Non dimittam te, nisi benedixeris mihi]]. Or, That he might overcome his adversaries, the men who were hostile to him; and above all, that he might overcome the invisible enemies of his salvation. Hence the angel said to him: [[Gen 32:28|if thou hast been strong against God, how much more shalt thou prevail against men?|Si contra Deum fortis fuisti, quanto magis contra homines prævalebis?]] In Genesis also Jacob says to Joseph: [[Gen 48:22|I give thee a portion above thy brethren, which|Do tibi partem unam extra fratres tuos, quam]] […] [[Osee 12:3|by his strength he had success with an angel|tudine sua directus est cum angelo]] [some words are lost here at the foot of the column: the rest of Gen 48:22 and the opening of the quotation from Osee]: [[Osee 12:4|And he prevailed over the angel, and was strengthened: he wept, and made supplication to him|et invaluit ad angelum, et confortatus est; flevit, et rogavit eum]]. [[10:12|and know|Et sciret]], that is, that he might experience in himself, through the helps shown him by God, and know more clearly from a fuller divine illumination, [[10:12|that wisdom is mightier than all|quoniam omnium potentior est sapientia]], the uncreated Wisdom, which is truly almighty and grants victory to her worshippers at her pleasure.

paras.t: Hæc sapientia venditum justum non dereliquit, scilicet sanctum Joseph, quem fratres sui vendiderunt Ismaelitis; sed a peccatoribus liberavit eum, id est a fratribus tunc injustis, quorum aliqui volebant eum occidere; a Putiphare quoque et impia conjuge ejus, quando ab eis de adulterii attentatione accusabatur. Descenditque cum illo in foveam, id est in carceris lacum, gratiose adsistens ei ibidem, juxta illud: Fuit autem Dominus cum Joseph, misertusque illius, dedit ei gratiam in conspectu principis carceris. Et in vinculis non dereliquit eum: unde in Psalmo, Humiliaverunt in compedibus pedes ejus; donec afferret illi sceptrum regni, id est, ad regiam dignitatem eum proveheret, dando ei gratiam exponendi somnia Pharaonis: qui dixit ad Joseph, Uno tantum regni solio te præcedam; et rursus, Absque tuo imperio nullus movebit manum aut pedem in tota terra Ægypti; et potentiam adversus eos qui eum deprimebant. Tunc enim factus est superior atque potentior Putiphare et conjuge ejus, a quibus fuit incarceratus. Verumtamen pius et mitis Joseph non se vindicavit de eis: imo eorum filiam duxit uxorem, ut patet in Genesi. Et mendaces ostendit eos qui maculaverunt illum, id est, de præfato crimine eum mendaciter accusaverunt: quia tunc veritas rei cunctis innotuit. Et dedit illi claritatem æternam.
paras.en: [[10:13|She forsook not the just when he was sold|Hæc sapientia venditum justum non dereliquit]]: that is, holy Joseph, whom his brethren sold to the Ismaelites[[Gen 37:28||]]; [[10:13|but delivered him from sinners|sed a peccatoribus liberavit eum]], that is, from his brethren, then unjust, some of whom wished to kill him[[Gen 37:20||]]; and also from Putiphar and his wicked wife, when he was accused by them of attempted adultery[[Gen 39:17||]]. [[10:13|She went down with him into the pit|Descenditque cum illo in foveam]], that is, into the dungeon of the prison, graciously standing by him there, according to that text: [[Gen 39:21|But the Lord was with Joseph, and having mercy upon him gave him favour in the sight of the chief keeper of the prison|Fuit autem Dominus cum Joseph, misertusque illius, dedit ei gratiam in conspectu principis carceris]]. [[10:14|And in bands she left him not|Et in vinculis non dereliquit eum]]: whence in the Psalm, [[Ps 104:18|They humbled his feet in fetters|Humiliaverunt in compedibus pedes ejus]]; [[10:14|till she brought him the sceptre of the kingdom|donec afferret illi sceptrum regni]], that is, till she raised him to kingly dignity, by giving him the grace to interpret the dreams of Pharao[[Gen 41:25||]], who said to Joseph: [[Gen 41:40|only in the kingly throne will I be above thee|Uno tantum regni solio te præcedam]]; and again, [[Gen 41:44|without thy commandment no man shall move hand or foot in all the land of Egypt|Absque tuo imperio nullus movebit manum aut pedem in tota terra Ægypti]]; [[10:14|and power against those that oppressed him|et potentiam adversus eos qui eum deprimebant]]. For then he was made higher and mightier than Putiphar and his wife, by whom he had been imprisoned[[Gen 39:19||]][[Gen 39:20||]]. Yet the kind and gentle Joseph did not avenge himself on them: nay rather, he took their daughter to wife, as is plain in Genesis[[Gen 41:50||]] [Denis takes Putiphar, Joseph's master, to be the Putiphare, priest of Heliopolis, whose daughter Aseneth Joseph married; the marriage itself is told at Gen 41:45]. [[10:14|And shewed them to be liars that had accused him|Et mendaces ostendit eos qui maculaverunt illum]] [*maculaverunt*, literally "stained" him], that is, who had lyingly accused him of the crime spoken of: for then the truth of the matter became known to all. [[10:14|And gave him everlasting glory|Et dedit illi claritatem æternam]].

paras.t: Hæc populum justum et semen sine querela liberavit a nationibus, quæ illum opprimebant: id est, sapientia liberavit Israeliticum populum de manu Ægyptiorum, a quibus gravissime premebantur laboribus durissimis, irrisionibus, et flagellis, atque necatione infantium. Porro populus ille Israel, vocatur justus et semen sine querela, id est absque reprehensibilitate vitiorum, denominando totum a parte: quoniam aliqui justi et sancti inter eos fuerunt. Attamen pro majori parte fuerunt valde imperfecti ac duræ cervicis.
paras.en: [[10:15|She delivered the just people, and blameless seed, from the nations that oppressed them|Hæc populum justum et semen sine querela liberavit a nationibus, quæ illum opprimebant]]: that is, wisdom delivered the Israelite people from the hand of the Egyptians, by whom they were most grievously oppressed with the hardest labours[[Ex 1:14||]], with mockeries[[Ex 1:13||]] and scourges, and with the slaying of their infants[[Ex 1:22||]]. Now that people Israel is called [[10:15|just|justus]] and [[10:15|blameless seed|semen sine querela]] [*sine querela*, literally "without complaint"], that is, without reproach for vices, naming the whole from the part [the figure called synecdoche]: since some among them were just and holy. Yet for the greater part they were very imperfect and stiff-necked[[Ex 32:9||]][[Ex 33:3||]][[Ex 33:5||]][[Ex 34:9||]][[Deut 9:6||]][[Deut 9:13||]][[Deut 31:27||]].

paras.t: Intravit sapientia ista in animam servi Dei, videlicet Moysis, quem illuminavit et confortavit, et misit ad educendum filios Israel: et stetit Moyses contra reges horrendos, id est contra Pharaonem ac principes ejus: qui et in Psalmo reges vocantur, quo legitur: Edidit terra eorum ranas, in penetralibus regum ipsorum; in portentis et signis, id est magnis et terribilibus prodigiis, plagis et ultionibus, quas miraculose fecit contra Ægyptios.
paras.en: [[10:16|She entered into the soul of the servant of God|Intravit sapientia ista in animam servi Dei]], namely of Moses, whom she enlightened and strengthened, and sent to lead out the children of Israel[[Ex 3:1||]][[Ex 4:1||]][[Ex 6:1||]]: and Moses [[10:16|stood against dreadful kings|stetit Moyses contra reges horrendos]] [in the text it is wisdom that stood; Denis makes Moses the subject], that is, against Pharao and his princes[[Ex 8:20||]][[Ex 9:13||]], who are also called kings in the Psalm, where we read: [[Ps 104:30|Their land brought forth frogs, in the inner chambers of their kings|Edidit terra eorum ranas, in penetralibus regum ipsorum]]; [[10:16|in wonders and signs|in portentis et signis]], that is, in great and terrible prodigies, plagues and punishments, which he wrought miraculously against the Egyptians[[Ex 7:1||]][[Ex 12:1||]] [the margin gives Exod. vii–x, xii: the plagues of Egypt].

paras.t: Et reddidit justis mercedem laborum suorum, id est, filiis Israel contulit spolia Ægyptiorum. Nempe, ut legitur in Exodo, fecerunt filii Israel sicut præceperat eis Dominus, et petierunt ab Ægyptiis vasa argentea et aurea, vestemque plurimam, et spoliaverunt Ægyptios. Et juste id actum: tum quoniam omnia sunt Dei, et potest ea dare cui voluerit; tum quia Ægyptii injuste gravaverant filios Israel multis laboribus, nec eos remuneraverunt. Ideo Deus hoc modo reddidit illis mercedem laborum suorum. Quod etiam de terra promissionis, quam contulit eis, accipi potest. Verumtamen dedit eis spiritualia præmia multo præstantiora, pro tanta patientia atque laboribus patienter exhibitis.
paras.en: [[10:17|And she rendered to the just the wages of their labours|Et reddidit justis mercedem laborum suorum]], that is, she bestowed on the children of Israel the spoils of the Egyptians. For, as we read in Exodus, [[Ex 12:50|the children of Israel did as the Lord had commanded|fecerunt filii Israel sicut præceperat eis Dominus]] them, [[Ex 12:35|and they asked of the Egyptians vessels of silver and gold, and very much raiment|et petierunt ab Ægyptiis vasa argentea et aurea, vestemque plurimam]], [[Ex 12:36|and they stripped the Egyptians|et spoliaverunt Ægyptios]] [the margin gives Exod. xii, 50, 35, 36; in 12:35 it is Moses who had commanded them]. And this was justly done: both because all things are God's, and he can give them to whom he will; and because the Egyptians had unjustly burdened the children of Israel with many labours, and had not paid them. Therefore God in this way rendered them [[10:17|the wages of their labours|mercedem laborum suorum]]. This can also be taken of the land of promise, which he bestowed on them. Yet he gave them spiritual rewards far more excellent, for so great a patience and for labours patiently borne.

paras.t: Et deduxit illos in via mirabili, id est per desertum illud horribile, in quo ante nemo transierat: in quo, sicut in Deuteronomio legitur, erant diversa serpentium genera et animalia venenosa: quæ tamen filiis Israel justis non nocuerunt. Ostendit quoque eis mirabiliter viam per columnam nubis in die, et per columnam ignis in nocte, ut in Exodo recitatur. Hinc subditur: et fuit illis in velamento die, id est, nubem concessit eis, per quam contra solis ardorem operiebantur, refrigeriumque habebant in die, et in luce stellarum nocte, id est, per columnam ignis illuminavit eos in nocte, quasi per lunam et stellas.
paras.en: [[10:17|And conducted them in a wonderful way|Et deduxit illos in via mirabili]], that is, through that horrible desert, through which no one had passed before: in which, as we read in Deuteronomy, there were divers kinds of serpents and venomous animals[[Deut 8:15||]], which nevertheless did not harm the just children of Israel. She also shewed them the way wonderfully by a pillar of cloud by day, and by a pillar of fire by night, as is recounted in Exodus[[Ex 13:21||]]. Hence it is added: [[10:17|and she was to them for a covert by day|et fuit illis in velamento die]], that is, she granted them the cloud, by which they were covered against the heat of the sun and had refreshment by day; [[10:17|and for the light of stars by night|et in luce stellarum nocte]], that is, she lit them by night through the pillar of fire, as though by the moon and stars.

paras.t: Et transtulit illos per mare Rubrum, id est per desiccatum fundum maris illius divisi: quod stetit ut murus ab utroque pertranseuntium latere, prout in Exodo plene describitur. Denique mare illud vocatur Rubrum, non quod aqua illa sit rubea, sed quia rubea apparet, propter rubeum fundum, cujus terra et saxa dicuntur rubea. Et transvexit illos per aquam nimiam, id est per fundum siccum copiosæ aquæ illius, ut dictum est; inimicos autem illorum, puta Ægyptios, demersit in mare: prout in Exodo legitur.
paras.en: [[10:18|And she brought them through the Red Sea|Et transtulit illos per mare Rubrum]], that is, over the dried-up bed of that sea, divided, which stood like a wall on either side of those passing through, as is fully described in Exodus[[Ex 14:21||]][[Ex 14:22||]][[Ex 14:29||]]. Now that sea is called Red, not because its water is red, but because it appears red, on account of its red bed, whose earth and stones are said to be red. [[10:18|And carried them over through a great water|Et transvexit illos per aquam nimiam]], that is, over the dry bed of that abundant water, as has been said; [[10:19|but their enemies|inimicos autem illorum]], namely the Egyptians, [[10:19|she drowned in the sea|demersit in mare]], as we read in Exodus[[Ex 14:27||]][[Ex 14:28||]].

paras.t: Et ab altitudine inferorum eduxit illos, id est de profunditate inferni. Per hoc enim quod liberavit eos de morte corporali, quam incidissent nisi miraculose continuisset aquas in suo situ, ne caderent super ipsos; liberavit et eos de inferis, in quos animæ eorum descendissent, si mortui tunc fuissent. Sunt equidem quatuor loca inferni, videlicet locus damnatorum, purgatorium, limbus patrum, et limbus puerorum. Et ad aliquem locorum illorum animæ descendissent. Juxta quem sensum apud Danielem legitur: Benedicite, Anania, Azaria, Misael, Domino, quia eruit nos de inferno: in Ecclesiastico quoque, Liberasti me de altitudine ventris inferi. Vel, Ab altitudine inferorum, id est gravissimarum afflictionum. Solet autem in Scripturis altitudo pro profunditate accipi, juxta illud in Psalmo, Veni in altitudinem maris; et apud Joannem, Puteus altus est.
paras.en: [[10:19|And from the depth of hell she brought them out|Et ab altitudine inferorum eduxit illos]], that is, from the deep of hell. For in delivering them from bodily death, into which they would have fallen had she not miraculously held the waters in their place, so that they should not fall upon them, she also delivered them from hell, into which their souls would have gone down had they died then. For there are four places of hell [*infernus*, the underworld in general, not only the place of the damned]: namely the place of the damned, purgatory, the limbo of the Fathers [where the just of the Old Testament awaited Christ], and the limbo of children [of those who die unbaptized]. And their souls would have gone down to one of those places. In this sense we read in Daniel: [[Dan 3:88|O Ananias, Azarias, Misael, bless ye the Lord|Benedicite, Anania, Azaria, Misael, Domino]], [[Dan 3:88|for he hath delivered us from hell|quia eruit nos de inferno]]; and in Ecclesiasticus too: [[Ecclus 51:4|Thou hast delivered me|Liberasti me]] [[Ecclus 51:7|from the depth of the belly of hell|de altitudine ventris inferi]]. Or, [[10:19|from the depth of hell|Ab altitudine inferorum]], that is, of most grievous afflictions. Now in the Scriptures *altitudo* [literally "height"] is often taken for depth, according to that in the Psalm: [[Ps 68:3|I am come into the depth of the sea|Veni in altitudinem maris]]; and in John: [[John 4:11|the well is deep|Puteus altus est]].

paras.t: Ideo justi tulerunt spolia impiorum. Circa hoc dicunt quidam Hebræi, aliqui quoque Catholici, quod, submersis Ægyptiis, et ad littus ejectis, filii Israel nudaverunt eos armis, et omnibus pretiosis quæ secum detulerunt, et quod spoliatio ista fuit major quam prima. Et juxta hoc dicere oportet, quod filii Israel exierunt mare Rubrum in eodem littore in quo illud introierunt: cujus oppositum Josephus tenet. Quid autem circa hoc sentiendum potius videatur, super Exodum scripsi. Glossa vero exponit istud de prima spoliatione.
paras.en: [[10:19|Therefore the just took the spoils of the wicked|Ideo justi tulerunt spolia impiorum]]. On this some Hebrews, and some Catholics too, say that when the Egyptians had been drowned and cast up on the shore, the children of Israel stripped them of their arms and of all the precious things they had brought with them, and that this spoiling was greater than the first. And on this view one must say that the children of Israel came out of the Red Sea on the same shore by which they had gone into it: the opposite of which Josephus holds. What should rather be thought about this I have written on Exodus[[Ex 14:31||]]. The Gloss, however, explains this of the first spoiling.

paras.t: Et decantaverunt, Domine, nomen sanctum tuum, id est, te Dominum laudaverunt cum cantico: quia tunc Moyses et filii Israel cecinerunt, dicentes: Cantemus Domino; gloriose enim magnificatus est, equum et ascensorem dejecit in mare. Moyses tamen totum canticum illud composuit metrice, et editum docuit filios Israel: et forsitan præcinebat eis, quemadmodum Maria soror sua, feminis, prout in Exodo scriptum est. Et victricem manum, id est omnipotentiam tuam, qua vicisti Ægyptios, laudaverunt pariter: quoniam sapientia aperuit os mutorum, id est, increata Sapientia excitavit tunc Israelitas ad Dei præconium: qui ante a laudibus Dei quasi muti fuerunt, nec contra Ægyptios oppressores suos loqui audebant: et forsan aliqui naturaliter muti, tunc supernaturaliter loqui ac Deum laudare exorsi sunt; et linguas infantium fecit disertas, id est, parvulos Hebræorum fecit in laude Dei facundos: et forsitan anticipatus est in quibusdam infantibus linguæ usus in laude hac Dei.
paras.en: [[10:20|And they sung to thy holy name, O Lord|Et decantaverunt, Domine, nomen sanctum tuum]], that is, they praised thee, the Lord, with a canticle: for then Moses and the children of Israel sang, saying: [[Ex 15:1|Let us sing to the Lord: for he is gloriously magnified, the horse and the rider he hath thrown into the sea|Cantemus Domino; gloriose enim magnificatus est, equum et ascensorem dejecit in mare]]. Moses, however, composed that whole canticle in metre, and when he had made it he taught it to the children of Israel: and perhaps he led them in the singing, as Mary his sister led the women, as is written in Exodus[[Ex 15:20||]][[Ex 15:21||]]. [[10:20|And they praised with one accord|laudaverunt pariter]] [[10:20|thy victorious hand|Et victricem manum]], that is, thy almighty power, by which thou didst overcome the Egyptians; [[10:21|for wisdom opened the mouth of the dumb|quoniam sapientia aperuit os mutorum]], that is, the uncreated Wisdom then stirred up the Israelites to the praise of God: who before had been as it were dumb as to the praises of God, and dared not speak against the Egyptians their oppressors; and perhaps some who were dumb by nature then began supernaturally to speak and to praise God. [[10:21|And made the tongues of infants eloquent|et linguas infantium fecit disertas]], that is, she made the little ones of the Hebrews eloquent in the praise of God: and perhaps in some infants the use of the tongue came before its time in this praise of God.

paras.t: Direxit opera eorum, id est facta Israelitarum, in manibus Prophetæ sancti, id est per obsequium et ducatum, per doctrinam atque miracula Moysis, qui fuit illorum director, doctor, legislator ac princeps.
paras.en: [[Wis 11:1|She prospered their works|Direxit opera eorum]] [*direxit*, literally "directed"], that is, the deeds of the Israelites, [[Wis 11:1|in the hands of the holy prophet|in manibus Prophetæ sancti]], that is, through the service and leadership, the teaching and the miracles of Moses, who was their director, teacher, lawgiver and prince.

paras.t: Insuper, quoniam multa hujus capituli verba cantat Ecclesia de beatissimis martyribus et confessoribus sanctis, tangendum est breviter qualiter illis conveniant verba ista.
paras.en: Moreover, since the Church sings many words of this chapter of the most blessed martyrs and of the holy confessors, we must touch briefly on how these words befit them.

paras.t: Justum deduxit Dominus per vias rectas, id est per observantiam præceptorum seu evangelicorum consiliorum, de loco hujus exsilii ad patriam Beatorum. Quemadmodum autem infantuli nequeunt ambulare nisi ducantur, seu parvo curriculo innitantur; sic fideles indigent indesinenter juvari, sustentari, ac duci a Deo, ne semitas exeant æquitatis. Alioqui regiam viam cito relinquerent, declinando ad dexteram vel sinistram. Ideo orat vir sanctus: Deduc me, Domine, in via tua; et, Gressus meos dirige secundum eloquium tuum. Et ostendit illi regnum Dei, dando ei gratiam contemplandi ac prægustandi gaudia regni cœlestis. Et dedit illi scientiam sanctorum, id est intelligentiam scripturarum Apostolorum, Evangelistarum, ac Prophetarum, vel illuminationem angelorum sanctorum; donum quoque scientiæ, quod infunditur cordibus omnium electorum. Honestavit illum in laboribus, id est, actibus virtuosis fecit eum studiose, fructuose, ac perseveranter intentum; et complevit labores illius, perducendo eos ad finem beatum.
paras.en: The Lord [[10:10|conducted the just|Justum deduxit]] [[10:10|through the right ways|per vias rectas]] [the verse as the Church sings it: *Justum deduxit Dominus per vias rectas*], that is, through the keeping of the commandments, or of the evangelical counsels, from the place of this exile to the fatherland of the Blessed. For as little children cannot walk unless they are led, or lean on a little go-cart [*curriculum*, a small wheeled frame on which a child learns to walk], so the faithful need without ceasing to be helped, upheld and led by God, lest they go out of the paths of equity. Otherwise they would soon leave the king's highway, turning aside to the right hand or to the left. Therefore the holy man prays: [[Ps 85:11|Conduct me, O Lord, in thy way|Deduc me, Domine, in via tua]]; and, [[Ps 118:133|Direct my steps according to thy word|Gressus meos dirige secundum eloquium tuum]]. [[10:10|And shewed him the kingdom of God|Et ostendit illi regnum Dei]], by giving him the grace to contemplate and to foretaste the joys of the heavenly kingdom. [[10:10|And gave him the knowledge of the holy things|Et dedit illi scientiam sanctorum]] [*scientia sanctorum* may mean the knowledge of holy things or of the saints; Denis here takes it of the saints], that is, understanding of the writings of the Apostles, Evangelists and Prophets, or the enlightening of the holy angels; and also the gift of knowledge, which is poured into the hearts of all the elect. [[10:10|Made him honourable in his labours|Honestavit illum in laboribus]], that is, made him intent on virtuous acts, zealously, fruitfully and perseveringly; [[10:10|and accomplished his labours|et complevit labores illius]], bringing them to a blessed end.

paras.t: In fraude circumvenientium illum adfuit: id est, a fraudibus invisibilium ac visibilium hostium ac tyrannorum eripuit eum ac præservavit, per illuminationem et directionem internam, per inspirationem angelicam; et honestum fecit illum, id est spiritualiter locupletem, totique mundo venerabilem, canonizando eumdem, et per diversa miracula Sanctum suum mirificando.
paras.en: [[10:11|In the deceit of them that overreached him, she stood by him|In fraude circumvenientium illum adfuit]]: that is, she rescued and preserved him from the frauds of enemies and tyrants, invisible and visible, by inward enlightening and direction, by the inspiration of angels; [[10:11|and made him honourable|et honestum fecit illum]], that is, spiritually rich and venerable to the whole world, by his canonization, and by making her Saint wonderful through divers miracles[[Ps 4:4||]].

paras.t: Custodivit illum ab inimicis præfatis, non ut eum non persequerentur aut trucidarent, sed ne per impatientiam aut aliam culpam corrueret; et a seductoribus, qui conati sunt per blandimenta et vana promissa, aut philosophica argumenta, vel comminationes et pœnarum acerbitates decipere Christi electos, tutavit illum, per sapientiam salutarem atque constantiam. Et certamen forte dedit illi, ut vinceret: quia contra diabolum, mundum et carnem jussit eum fortiter præliari ac prævalere: Nolite, inquiens, timere eos qui corpus occidunt. Non enim coronatur, nisi qui legitime certaverit. Et sciret quoniam omnium potentior est sapientia, id est, victoriam suam non sibi ipsi, sed Christo adscriberet, a quo sibi promissum fuit: Ego dabo vobis os et sapientiam, cui non poterunt resistere et contradicere omnes adversarii vestri.
paras.en: [[10:12|She kept him safe from his enemies|Custodivit illum ab inimicis]] already named: not so that they should not persecute or slaughter him, but so that he should not fall through impatience or some other fault; [[10:12|and she defended him|tutavit illum]] [[10:12|from seducers|a seductoribus]], who strove by flatteries and vain promises, or by philosophical arguments, or by threats and the bitterness of torments, to deceive the elect of Christ, by saving wisdom and constancy. [[10:12|And gave him a strong conflict, that he might overcome|Et certamen forte dedit illi, ut vinceret]]: for he bade him fight bravely against the devil, the world and the flesh, and prevail, saying: [[Matt 10:28|Fear ye not them that kill the body|Nolite, inquiens, timere eos qui corpus occidunt]]. For a man [[2 Tim 2:5|is not crowned, except he strive lawfully|Non enim coronatur, nisi qui legitime certaverit]]. [[10:12|And know that wisdom is mightier than all|Et sciret quoniam omnium potentior est sapientia]], that is, that he should ascribe his victory not to himself but to Christ, by whom it was promised him: [[Luke 21:15|I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all your adversaries shall not be able to resist and gainsay|Ego dabo vobis os et sapientiam, cui non poterunt resistere et contradicere omnes adversarii vestri]].

paras.t: Hæc venditum justum non dereliquit. Nam multi Sancti fuerunt perfidis venditi, sed a Sapientia summa nequaquam relicti. Sed a peccatoribus liberavit eum per patientiam et glorificationem in cœlis æternam. Descenditque cum illo in foveam. Certum est quod felicissimis martyribus in omni eorum cruciatu acerrimo gratiosissime adstitit. Donec afferret illi sceptrum regni, id est, in cœlesti gloria coronaret.
paras.en: [[10:13|She forsook not the just when he was sold|Hæc venditum justum non dereliquit]]. For many Saints were sold to the faithless, but in no way forsaken by the supreme Wisdom. [[10:13|But delivered him from sinners|Sed a peccatoribus liberavit eum]], through patience and through everlasting glorification in heaven. [[10:13|She went down with him into the pit|Descenditque cum illo in foveam]]. It is certain that she stood most graciously by the most happy martyrs in all their sharpest torment. [[10:14|Till she brought him the sceptre of the kingdom|Donec afferret illi sceptrum regni]], that is, till she crowned him in heavenly glory.

paras.t: Hæc sapientia populum justum, videlicet christianum, liberavit a nationibus perfidorum.
paras.en: [[10:15|She delivered the just people|Hæc sapientia populum justum]], namely the Christian people, [[10:15|from the nations|liberavit a nationibus]] of the faithless.

paras.t: Reddidit Deus mercedem laborum Sanctorum suorum, id est, pro virtuosis eorum laboribus contulit ipsis copiosissimum præmium, etiam ultra condignum, nec solum in patria, sed etiam consolando, spiritualiterque ditando, et magnificando eos in via. Et deduxit illos in via mirabili, id est in conversatione sancta, perfecta, heroica, quæ super hominem est, et supernaturalis omnino; item, In via mirabili, id est in fide catholica et evangelica lege, quæ rationem transcendunt.
paras.en: God [[10:17|rendered to the just the wages of their labours|Reddidit Deus mercedem laborum Sanctorum suorum]] [Denis gives the verse as the Church sings it: *Reddidit Deus mercedem laborum sanctorum suorum*, "God hath rendered the wages of the labours of his saints"], that is, for their virtuous labours he bestowed on them a most plentiful reward, even beyond their desert, not only in the fatherland but also on the way [that is, in this life, while they are still wayfarers], by consoling them, enriching them spiritually, and making them great. [[10:17|And conducted them in a wonderful way|Et deduxit illos in via mirabili]], that is, in a holy, perfect, heroic manner of life, which is above man and wholly supernatural; again, [[10:17|in a wonderful way|In via mirabili]], that is, in the Catholic faith and the law of the Gospel, which transcend reason.

paras.t: Et fuit illis in velamento die, id est, in prosperis et jucundis, et in omni spirituali profectu, qui dies vocatur interior, obumbravit eis per gratiam humilitatis, ne extollerentur; et in luce stellarum nocte, id est, in adversis et asperis, ac subtractione consolationis internæ, contulit eis lumen quoddam sidereum, ad considerandum quod in tali eventu patientia sit habenda, ac divina pietas invocanda, ejusque consolatio postulanda, vana quoque consolatio contemnenda, ne dejiciantur: pensantes quod per multas tribulationes oporteat nos intrare regnum cœlorum; et quod ait Scriptura: In die bonorum, ne immemor sis malorum: et in die malorum, ne immemor sis bonorum. Amplius, Fuit illis in velamento die, id est, in luce vitæ præsentis eos benigne protexit: juxta quod scriptum est, Protegar in velamento alarum tuarum; et rursus, In velamento alarum tuarum exsultabo. Et in luce stellarum nocte, id est, tempore mortis diræ, luce miserationis supernæ corda eorum perfudit et illustravit, ut in statu gratiæ et conversione ad Deum discederent de hac vita.
paras.en: [[10:17|And she was to them for a covert by day|Et fuit illis in velamento die]], that is, in prosperity and pleasant things, and in all spiritual progress, which is called the inward day, she overshadowed them with the grace of humility, lest they be lifted up; [[10:17|and for the light of stars by night|et in luce stellarum nocte]], that is, in adversity and hardship, and in the withdrawal of inward consolation, she bestowed on them a certain starry light, so that they consider that in such a case patience must be had, the divine mercy called upon, its consolation asked for, and vain consolation despised, lest they be cast down: weighing that [[Acts 14:21|through many tribulations we must enter|per multas tribulationes oporteat nos intrare]] into the kingdom of heaven; and what the Scripture says: [[Ecclus 11:27|In the day of good things be not unmindful of evils: and in the day of evils be not unmindful of good things|In die bonorum, ne immemor sis malorum: et in die malorum, ne immemor sis bonorum]]. Further, [[10:17|she was to them for a covert by day|Fuit illis in velamento die]], that is, in the light of the present life she kindly protected them, according to what is written: [[Ps 60:5|I shall be protected under the covert of thy wings|Protegar in velamento alarum tuarum]]; and again, [[Ps 62:8|I will rejoice under the cover of thy wings|In velamento alarum tuarum exsultabo]]. [[10:17|And for the light of stars by night|Et in luce stellarum nocte]], that is, in the time of dreadful death, she flooded and lit up their hearts with the light of heavenly mercy, so that they departed this life in the state of grace and turned to God.

paras.t: Transtulit illos per mare Rubrum, id est, per Baptismum, quem significavit mare Rubrum, fecit de filiis iræ filios adoptionis divinæ ac sanctæ Ecclesiæ, dicente Apostolo: Eripuit nos de præsenti sæculo nequam, et transtulit in regnum Filii dilectionis suæ. Unde et ipsa Sapientia dixit: Nisi quis renatus fuerit ex aqua et Spiritu Sancto, non potest introire in regnum Dei. Vel, Per mare Rubrum, id est per imitativam dominicæ passionis meditationem, quæ compendiose ducit ad gloriam. Rursus, Per mare Rubrum, id est per martyrii palmam, seu quotidianam mortificationem salubrem. Et transvexit illos per aquam nimiam, id est per abundantiam tribulationum: quemadmodum scriptum est. Transivimus per ignem et aquam; itemque, Elevaverunt flumina fluctus suos, a vocibus aquarum multarum. Potest etiam per nimiam aquam, abundantia gratiæ designari. Unde ait Salvator: Qui biberit ex aqua quam ego dabo ei, non sitiet in æternum; sed aqua quam ego dabo ei, fiet in eo fons aquæ salientis in vitam æternam.
paras.en: [[10:18|She brought them through the Red Sea|Transtulit illos per mare Rubrum]], that is, through Baptism, which the Red Sea signified, she made of [[Eph 2:3|children of wrath|filiis iræ]] children of the divine adoption and of holy Church, as the Apostle says: He [[Col 1:13|hath delivered us|Eripuit nos]] [[Gal 1:4|from this present wicked world|de præsenti sæculo nequam]], [[Col 1:13|and hath translated us into the kingdom of the Son of his love|et transtulit in regnum Filii dilectionis suæ]] [Denis joins Col 1:13 and Gal 1:4 into one sentence]. Whence Wisdom herself said: [[John 3:5|unless a man be born again of water and the Holy Ghost, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God|Nisi quis renatus fuerit ex aqua et Spiritu Sancto, non potest introire in regnum Dei]]. Or, [[10:18|through the Red Sea|Per mare Rubrum]], that is, through a meditation on the Lord's passion that imitates it, which leads by a short way to glory. Again, [[10:18|through the Red Sea|Per mare Rubrum]], that is, through the palm of martyrdom, or a wholesome daily mortification. [[10:18|And carried them over through a great water|Et transvexit illos per aquam nimiam]], that is, through an abundance of tribulations, as it is written: [[Ps 65:12|We have passed through fire and water|Transivimus per ignem et aquam]]; and again, [[Ps 92:3|The floods have lifted up their waves|Elevaverunt flumina fluctus suos]], [[Ps 92:4|with the noise of many waters|a vocibus aquarum multarum]]. By [[10:18|a great water|nimiam aquam]] an abundance of grace may also be signified. Whence the Saviour says: [[John 4:13|he that shall drink of the water that I will give him shall not thirst for ever|Qui biberit ex aqua quam ego dabo ei, non sitiet in æternum]]; [[John 4:14|But the water that I will give him shall become in him a fountain of water, springing up into life everlasting|sed aqua quam ego dabo ei, fiet in eo fons aquæ salientis in vitam æternam]].

paras.t: Inimicos autem illorum, scilicet reprobos et iniquos, demersit in mare, id est, in vitiorum suorum inquietudine ac amaritudine ipsos damnavit. Impii etenim quasi mare fervens, quod quiescere non potest, ut in Isaia asseritur. Et in afflictionum gravissimarum profunditatem illos projecit. Et ab altitudine inferorum eduxit illos, id est, electos eripuit de potestate infernalium tenebrarum, a jugo peccati, a statu damnationis: in quo quandoque fuerunt, sicut ait Apostolus: Fuimus enim et nos aliquando insipientes, odibiles, odientes invicem.
paras.en: [[10:19|But their enemies|Inimicos autem illorum]], namely the reprobate and wicked, [[10:19|she drowned in the sea|demersit in mare]], that is, she condemned them in the restlessness and bitterness of their own vices. For [[Is 57:20|the wicked are like the raging sea, which cannot rest|Impii etenim quasi mare fervens, quod quiescere non potest]], as is asserted in Isaias. And she cast them into the depth of most grievous afflictions. [[10:19|And from the depth of hell she brought them out|Et ab altitudine inferorum eduxit illos]], that is, she rescued the elect from the power of the infernal darkness, from the yoke of sin, from the state of damnation, in which they once were, as the Apostle says: [[Tit 3:3|For we ourselves also were some time unwise|Fuimus enim et nos aliquando insipientes]], [[Tit 3:3|hateful and hating one another|odibiles, odientes invicem]].

paras.t: Ideo justi tulerunt spolia impiorum, id est, peccatores abstraxerunt dæmonibus, et converterunt eos ad Christum, gratiam quam acceperant communicantes proximis suis: quod viri sancti copiose fecerunt, orando, prædicando, exemplariterque vivendo, ipsisque gratiam conversionis promerendo per superabundantem meritorum suorum erogationem, prout loquitur Paulus: Suppleo ea quæ desunt passionum Christi, pro corpore ejus, quod est Ecclesia. Et denuo: Omnia, inquit, sustineo propter electos, ut et ipsi consequantur salutem. De his spoliis scriptum est in Isaia: Fortium dividet spolia; in Evangelio quoque: Quum fortis armatus custodit atrium suum, in pace sunt ea quæ possidet; si autem fortior illo supervenerit, spolia ejus distribuet.
paras.en: [[10:19|Therefore the just took the spoils of the wicked|Ideo justi tulerunt spolia impiorum]], that is, they drew sinners away from the demons and converted them to Christ, sharing with their neighbours the grace they had received: which holy men have done abundantly, by praying, by preaching and by living as an example, and by meriting for them the grace of conversion through the superabundant spending of their own merits, as Paul says: I [[Col 1:24|fill up those things that are wanting of the sufferings of Christ|Suppleo ea quæ desunt passionum Christi]], [[Col 1:24|for his body, which is the church|pro corpore ejus, quod est Ecclesia]]. And again he says: [[2 Tim 2:10|I endure all things for the sake of the elect, that they also may obtain the salvation|Omnia, inquit, sustineo propter electos, ut et ipsi consequantur salutem]]. Of these spoils it is written in Isaias: [[Is 53:12|he shall divide the spoils of the strong|Fortium dividet spolia]]; and in the Gospel too: [[Luke 11:21|When a strong man armed keepeth his court, those things are in peace which he possesseth.|Quum fortis armatus custodit atrium suum, in pace sunt ea quæ possidet]] [[Luke 11:22|But if a stronger than he come upon him|si autem fortior illo supervenerit]], he [[Luke 11:22|will distribute his spoils|spolia ejus distribuet]].

paras.t: Et decantaverunt, Domine, nomen sanctum tuum, gratias agentes Deo Patri per Filium ejus, dicentes illud Apocalypsis: Dignus es, Domine, accipere librum, et solvere signacula ejus: quoniam occisus es, et redemisti nos Deo in sanguine tuo. Et rursus ibidem: Dignus est Agnus qui occisus est, accipere virtutem, et divinitatem, et sapientiam, et fortitudinem, et honorem, et gloriam, et benedictionem. Et victricem manum tuam, qua aerias debellasti potestates, laudaverunt pariter, illud concinentes: Benedictio, et claritas, et sapientia, et gratiarum actio, honor, et virtus, et fortitudo Deo nostro in sæcula sæculorum.
paras.en: [[10:20|And they sung to thy holy name, O Lord|Et decantaverunt, Domine, nomen sanctum tuum]], giving thanks to God the Father through his Son, saying that verse of the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 5:9|Thou art worthy, O Lord, to take the book and to open the seals thereof: because thou wast slain and hast redeemed us to God, in thy blood|Dignus es, Domine, accipere librum, et solvere signacula ejus: quoniam occisus es, et redemisti nos Deo in sanguine tuo]]. And again in the same place: [[Apoc 5:12|The Lamb that was slain is worthy to receive power and divinity and wisdom and strength and honour and glory and benediction|Dignus est Agnus qui occisus est, accipere virtutem, et divinitatem, et sapientiam, et fortitudinem, et honorem, et gloriam, et benedictionem]]. [[10:20|And they praised with one accord|laudaverunt pariter]] [[10:20|thy victorious hand|Et victricem manum tuam]], by which thou didst overthrow the powers of the air, singing together that verse: [[Apoc 7:12|Benediction and glory and wisdom and thanksgiving, honour and power and strength, to our God, for ever and ever|Benedictio, et claritas, et sapientia, et gratiarum actio, honor, et virtus, et fortitudo Deo nostro in sæcula sæculorum]].

paras.t: Quoniam sapientia aperuit os mutorum, id est, ora gentilium conversorum, qui muti erant a laudibus Dei, convertit in laudes ipsius, et prædicatores fecit ex eis, juxta illud in Psalmo: Lingua canum tuorum ex inimicis, ab ipso. Ora quoque Apostolorum et discipulorum, qui a tempore passionis Christi non audebant prædicare et apparere, aperuit gloriosissime in sancto Pentecostes die, misso et eis infuso Spiritu Sancto: quo facto, mox orsi sunt constantissime prædicare, multaque millia converterunt assidue. Corporaliter etiam Christus multos mutos fecit loquentes. Imo quamplures linguis eorum abscisis eloqui fecit et evangelizare. Et linguas infantium fecit disertas, scilicet in die Palmarum, quando pueri Hebræorum cantaverunt dicentes: Hosanna filio David! Benedictus qui venit in nomine Domini. Quando impletum est illud in Psalmo: Ex ore infantium et lactentium perfecisti laudem. Sed et multi infantuli in evangelica lege supernaturaliter sunt locuti.
paras.en: [[10:21|For wisdom opened the mouth of the dumb|Quoniam sapientia aperuit os mutorum]], that is, the mouths of the converted Gentiles, who were dumb as to the praises of God, she turned to his praises, and made preachers of them, according to that in the Psalm: [[Ps 67:24|the tongue of thy dogs|Lingua canum tuorum]] from among the enemies, from him [Denis reads *ex inimicis, ab ipso* of preachers made out of God's former enemies; the Douay-Rheims renders the verse "the tongue of thy dogs be red with the same"]. The mouths too of the Apostles and disciples, who from the time of Christ's passion dared not preach or show themselves, she opened most gloriously on the holy day of Pentecost, when the Holy Ghost was sent and poured into them[[Acts 2:4||]]: upon which they at once began to preach most steadfastly, and converted many thousands, one after another[[Acts 2:14||]][[Acts 2:41||]][[Acts 4:4||]]. Christ also made many who were bodily dumb speak[[Matt 9:33||]][[Matt 12:22||]][[Matt 15:30||]][[Mark 7:35||]][[Luke 11:14||]]. Nay more, he made very many speak and preach the Gospel when their tongues had been cut out. [[10:21|And made the tongues of infants eloquent|Et linguas infantium fecit disertas]], namely on Palm Sunday, when the children of the Hebrews sang, saying: [[Matt 21:9|Hosanna to the son of David: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord|Hosanna filio David! Benedictus qui venit in nomine Domini]]. Then was fulfilled that in the Psalm: [[Ps 8:3|Out of the mouth of infants and of sucklings thou hast perfected praise|Ex ore infantium et lactentium perfecisti laudem]]. And many little infants too, under the law of the Gospel, have spoken supernaturally.

paras.t: Direxit opera eorum, id est, opera Christianorum Deus Pater direxit, in manibus Prophetæ sancti, id est in virtute et gratia, in fide et lege, præceptis atque consiliis Christi: qui est magni consilii Angelus; et Propheta: de quo quidam vere dixerunt, Propheta magnus surrexit in nobis; et rursus, Hic est vere Propheta qui venturus est in mundum.
paras.en: [[Wis 11:1|She prospered their works|Direxit opera eorum]], that is, God the Father prospered the works of Christians, [[Wis 11:1|in the hands of the holy prophet|in manibus Prophetæ sancti]], that is, in the power and grace, in the faith and law, in the precepts and counsels of Christ: who is the Angel of great counsel[[Is 9:6||]] [so Isaias 9:6 reads in the Septuagint and in the Introit of the Mass of Christmas Day; the Vulgate has "Counsellor"]; and the Prophet, of whom some said truly: [[Luke 7:16|A great prophet is risen up among us|Propheta magnus surrexit in nobis]]; and again, [[John 6:14|This is of a truth the prophet that is to come into the world|Hic est vere Propheta qui venturus est in mundum]].

11.title: EXPLANATIO CAPITULI UNDECIMI : ITER FECERUNT PER DESERTA.
11.title_en: Explanation of the eleventh chapter: They went through wildernesses

paras.t: Beneficia æternæ et increatæ Sapientiæ exhibita populo Israel ex Ægypti terra educto, et ipsorum Ægyptiorum justæ punitiones hic recitantur.
paras.en: The benefits of the eternal and uncreated Wisdom shewn to the people of Israel when they had been led out of the land of Egypt, and the just punishments of the Egyptians themselves, are recounted here.

paras.t: Iter fecerunt filii Israel per Moysen educti, per deserta quæ non habitabantur. Quamvis enim fuerit ibi unum totale desertum, in quo pro maxima parte fuerunt pergentes, tamen illud in diversis partibus suis diversa sortitur vocabula: utpote desertum Ægypti, desertum Etham, desertum Pharan, desertum Sur, desertum Moab, desertumque Idumææ, ut patet in Exodo, etc. De quo legitur: Non dixerunt: Ubi est Dominus, qui ascendere nos fecit de terra Ægypti, qui traduxit nos per desertum, per terram inhabitabilem et inviam, per terram sitis et imaginem mortis, per terram in qua non ambulavit vir, neque habitavit homo? Et in locis deserti illius totalis fecerunt casas, id est tabernacula de arboribus: in cujus rei memoriam præcepit Dominus festum Tabernaculorum servari, ut in Levitico et Deuteronomio patet. Ad Hebræos quoque scribitur de Abraham: Fide demoratus est in terra repromissionis, tanquam in aliena, in casulis habitando cum Isaac et Jacob.
paras.en: [[11:2|They went|Iter fecerunt]], the children of Israel, led out by Moses, [[11:2|through wildernesses that were not inhabited|per deserta quæ non habitabantur]]. For although there was there one whole desert, through which for the most part they journeyed, yet in its different parts it bears different names: as the desert of Egypt, the desert of Etham, the desert of Pharan, the desert of Sur, the desert of Moab, and the desert of Idumea, as is plain in Exodus, etc. Of this desert we read: [[Jer 2:6|they have not said: Where is the Lord, that made us come up out of the land of Egypt? that led us through the desert, through a land uninhabited and unpassable, through a land of drought, and the image of death, through a land wherein no man walked, nor any man dwelt?|Non dixerunt: Ubi est Dominus, qui ascendere nos fecit de terra Ægypti, qui traduxit nos per desertum, per terram inhabitabilem et inviam, per terram sitis et imaginem mortis, per terram in qua non ambulavit vir, neque habitavit homo?]] [[11:2|and in desert places|Et in locis deserti]] of that whole wilderness [[11:2|they pitched their tents|fecerunt casas]], that is, tabernacles made of trees: in memory of which the Lord commanded the feast of Tabernacles to be kept, as is plain in Leviticus[[Lev 23:34||]] and Deuteronomy[[Deut 16:13||]]. In the Epistle to the Hebrews too it is written of Abraham: [[Heb 11:9|By faith he abode in the land of promise, as in a strange country, dwelling in cottages, with Isaac and Jacob|Fide demoratus est in terra repromissionis, tanquam in aliena, in casulis habitando cum Isaac et Jacob]].

paras.t: Steterunt contra hostes, et de inimicis se vindicaverunt. Hoc cœptum est fieri, quando, ut in Exodo legitur, Josue et missi cum eo, pugnaverunt contra Amalecitas, et eos in ore gladii fugere compulerunt.
paras.en: [[11:3|They stood against their enemies, and revenged themselves of their adversaries|Steterunt contra hostes, et de inimicis se vindicaverunt]]. This began to be done when, as we read in Exodus, Josue and those sent with him fought against the Amalecites[[Ex 17:9||]], and drove them to flight by the edge of the sword[[Ex 17:13||]].

paras.t: Sitierunt, et invocaverunt te, et data est illis aqua de petra altissima. Hoc contigit, quando in deserto Raphidim aqua defuit eis, et Deo jubente Moyses percussit petram Horeb: de qua mox aqua copiosa manavit, bibitque populus. Unde subjungitur: et requies sitis de lapide duro, id est cessatio a siti, seu sitis exstinctio, per hoc quod potaverunt aquam fluentem de saxo illo durissimo, prout præallegato Exodi narratur capitulo. Vocatur demum petra illa, altissima, vel quia alte sita, vel propter excellentiam tanti miraculi in ea peracti. Sed quomodo dicitur hic, Invocaverunt te? quum scriptum sit prætacto capitulo, quod jurgati sunt contra Moysen, et murmuraverunt contra eum: quibus et dixit: Cur tentatis Dominum? Et respondendum, quod quidam de melioribus simul cum Moyse Dominum invocaverunt: de quibus Dominus dixit ad Moysen, Nunc tecum de senioribus Israel.
paras.en: [[11:4|They were thirsty, and they called upon thee, and water was given them out of the high rock|Sitierunt, et invocaverunt te, et data est illis aqua de petra altissima]]. This happened when water failed them in the desert of Raphidim[[Ex 17:1||]], and at God's command Moses struck the rock Horeb[[Ex 17:6||]]: from which plentiful water presently flowed, and the people drank. Hence it is added: [[11:4|and a refreshment of their thirst out of the hard stone|et requies sitis de lapide duro]], that is, a ceasing from thirst, or the quenching of thirst, in that they drank the water that flowed from that hardest rock, as is told in the chapter of Exodus already cited. That rock, lastly, is called *high*, either because it stood high, or because of the excellence of so great a miracle wrought in it. But how is it said here, [[11:4|they called upon thee|Invocaverunt te]]? since it is written in the chapter already mentioned that they chode with Moses[[Ex 17:2||]] and murmured against him[[Ex 17:3||]]: and he said to them: [[Ex 17:2|Wherefore do you tempt the Lord|Cur tentatis Dominum]]? And the answer is that some of the better among them called upon the Lord together with Moses: of whom the Lord said to Moses, Now [[Ex 17:5|take with thee of the ancients of Israel|tecum de senioribus Israel]] [the print has *Nunc*, "now", where the Vulgate has *Sume*, "take"].

paras.t: Sequitur de pœnis Ægyptiorum. Per quæ enim pœnas passi sunt inimici illorum, id est Ægyptii adversarii Israelitarum: qui Ægyptii passi sunt sitim, quum Deus convertisset aquas eorum in sanguinem; a defectione potus sui, id est ex defectu aquæ quam solebant potare; et in eis, scilicet in aquis, quum abundarent filii Israel: quia in terra Gessen, in qua morabantur, aqua non fuit in sanguinem versa, ut loquitur Augustinus; lætati sunt de beneficiis Dei et abundantia potus.
paras.en: There follows the punishment of the Egyptians. [[11:5|For by what things their enemies were punished|Per quæ enim pœnas passi sunt inimici illorum]], that is, the Egyptians, the adversaries of the Israelites (these Egyptians suffered thirst when God had turned their waters into blood[[Ex 7:20||]] [the margin gives Exod. xvii, 20; the passage is Exod 7:20]), [[11:5|when their drink failed them|a defectione potus sui]], that is, through the want of the water they were used to drink; [[11:5|while the children of Israel abounded|quum abundarent filii Israel]] [[11:5|therewith|et in eis]], that is, with the waters (for in the land of Gessen, where they dwelt, the water was not turned into blood, as Augustine says), [[11:5|and rejoiced|lætati sunt]] in the benefits of God and the abundance of drink.

paras.t: Per hoc beneficium, quum illis deesset, id est, dum deesset Ægyptiis sufficientia potus, bene cum illis actum est, id est, cum filiis Israel factum est gratiose, quia non fuerunt plagati sicut Ægyptii. Unde Dominus ait: Percutiam aquam fluminis, et vertetur in sanguinem; pisces quoque qui sunt in flumine, morientur, et putrescent aquæ, et affligentur Ægyptii, bibentes aquam fluminis. Aliqui autem dicunt, quod etiam in terra Gessen aqua fuit in sanguinem commutata. Sed quando filii Israel hauserunt ex flumine, statim revertebatur sanguis ad aquæ naturam. De hoc super Exodum dictum est plenius.
paras.en: [[11:6|By the same things|Per hoc]] benefit, [[11:6|in their need|quum illis deesset]] [Denis takes these words of the Egyptians: "when it was lacking to them"], that is, while the Egyptians lacked enough to drink, they [[11:6|were benefited|bene cum illis actum est]], that is, it went graciously with the children of Israel, since they were not stricken as the Egyptians were. Hence the Lord says: [[Ex 7:17|I will strike with the rod, that is in my hand, the water of the river, and it shall be turned into blood|Percutiam aquam fluminis, et vertetur in sanguinem]]; [[Ex 7:18|And the fishes that are in the river, shall die, and the waters shall be corrupted, and the Egyptians shall be afflicted when they drink the water of the river|pisces quoque qui sunt in flumine, morientur, et putrescent aquæ, et affligentur Ægyptii, bibentes aquam fluminis]]. Some, however, say that in the land of Gessen too the water was changed into blood; but when the children of Israel drew from the river, the blood at once went back to the nature of water. This was said more fully on Exodus [the margin refers to Denis's commentary on Exodus, art. XII, towards the end].

paras.t: Nam pro fonte quidem sempiterni fluminis, id est pro aqua Nili instar fontis potabili: qui dicitur, flumen sempiternum, quia est unus de quatuor fluviis paradisi, et in Genesi vocatur Gehon: circumiens omnem terram Æthiopiæ, et ibi dicitur Gehon: inde autem in Ægyptum descendens, ubi Nilus vocatur, et per diversa loca ibidem dividitur: ut dictum est super Genesim. Humanum sanguinem, id est sanguinem in colore similem sanguini hominis, dedisti injustis, id est Ægyptiis, ad potandum, convertendo aquas eorum in sanguinem. Quam plagam juste perpessi sunt, quoniam peccaverunt infantulos Hebræorum submergendo in flumine.
paras.en: [[11:7|For instead of a fountain of an ever running river|Nam pro fonte quidem sempiterni fluminis]], that is, instead of the water of the Nile, drinkable like that of a spring: it is called an ever running river because it is one of the four rivers of paradise, and in Genesis it is called Gehon, [[Gen 2:13|that compasseth all the land of Ethiopia|circumiens omnem terram Æthiopiæ]], and there it is called Gehon; but coming down from there into Egypt, where it is called the Nile, it is divided there into divers places, as was said on Genesis. [[11:7|human blood|Humanum sanguinem]], that is, blood like the blood of a man in colour, [[11:7|thou gavest|dedisti]] [[11:7|to the unjust|injustis]], that is, to the Egyptians, to drink, by turning their waters into blood. This plague they justly suffered, since they had sinned by drowning the little ones of the Hebrews in the river[[Ex 1:22||]].

paras.t: Unde adjicitur: Qui, scilicet filii Israel, quum minuerentur in traductione infantium occisorum, id est, pauciores numero fierent, per hoc quod eorum infantes occidebantur per submersionem in Nilo, dedisti illis, puta Hebræis, abundantem aquam ad potandum, insperate, id est præter spem, vel non convertendo aquas terræ Gessen in sanguinem, vel sanguinem haustum ab eis reducendo in aquæ naturam;
