paras.en: [[17:16|For if any one were a husbandman, or a shepherd, or a labourer in the field|Si enim rusticus quis erat, aut pastor pecorum, aut agri laborum operarius]], that is, a tiller of the fields (and there were certainly many thousands such in Egypt), [[17:16|and was suddenly overtaken|præoccupatus]], that is, caught unawares, by that darkness, and had fallen into it in the field or anywhere else, [[17:16|he endured a necessity from which he could not fly|ineffugibilem sustinebat necessitatem]]: that is, he was inescapably forced to stay in that place, unable to get away, and unable to see where to go. For [[17:17|with one chain|Una enim catena]], that is, by one shutting in and holding fast, [[17:17|of darkness|tenebrarum illarum]] [[17:17|they were all bound together|omnes Ægyptii erant colligati]], unable to change their place: and they were so dazed and fearful that whatever they heard brought fear upon them: as a man in great fear is terrified by the sound of a leaf, or the scurrying of a mouse. Hence is added:

paras.t: Sive spiritus, id est ventus, sibilans, aut inter spissos arborum ramos avium sonus suavis, aut vis aquæ decurrentis nimium, id est sonus causatus ex cursu aquarum, aut sonus validus præcipitatarum petrarum, id est lapidum a sursum projectorum deorsum, aut ludentium animalium cursus invisus, id est factus extra intuitum Ægyptiorum illorum, aut mugientium valida bestiarum vox, aut resonans de altissimis montibus echo, utpote ex repercussione reflexus; deficientes faciebant illos præ timore, id est, debilitabant Ægyptios, qui ex prædominante timore jugiter suspicabantur sibi grandia imminere pericula.
paras.en: [[17:17|Whether it were|Sive]] the breath, that is, the wind, [[17:17|whistling|sibilans]], [[17:17|or the melodious voice of birds, among the spreading branches of trees|aut inter spissos arborum ramos avium sonus suavis]], [[17:17|or a fall of water running down with violence|aut vis aquæ decurrentis nimium]], that is, the sound caused by the running of waters, [[17:18|Or the mighty noise of stones tumbling down|aut sonus validus præcipitatarum petrarum]], that is, of stones flung from above downwards, [[17:18|or the running that could not be seen of beasts playing together|aut ludentium animalium cursus invisus]], that is, made out of the sight of those Egyptians, [[17:18|or the roaring voice of wild beasts|aut mugientium valida bestiarum vox]], [[17:18|or a rebounding echo from the highest mountains|aut resonans de altissimis montibus echo]], as being thrown back by reverberation; [[17:18|these things made them to swoon for fear|deficientes faciebant illos præ timore]], that is, they weakened the Egyptians, who out of the fear that had mastery over them were constantly suspecting that great dangers were hanging over them.

paras.t: Omnis enim orbis terrarum, id est totus mundus, limpido illuminabatur lumine, id est claro lumine solis, et non impeditis operibus continebatur : id est, proprios actus expedite naturaliterque exercuit, dempto territorio Ægyptiorum. Unde subjungitur :
paras.en: [[17:19|For the whole world|Omnis enim orbis terrarum]], that is, the entire world, [[17:19|was enlightened, with a clear light|limpido illuminabatur lumine]], that is, with the clear light of the sun, [[17:19|and none were hindered in their labours|et non impeditis operibus continebatur]]: that is, it carried on its own activities freely and in the way of nature, save for the territory of the Egyptians. Hence is added:

paras.t: Solis autem illis superposita erat gravis nox, durans per triduum. Alibi vero dies et nox consueto cursu fiebant. Imago tenebrarum, quæ superventura illis erat : id est, nox illa fuit figura, imago et signum infernalium tenebrarum : in quas erant descensuri post vitam hanc, quia non fuerunt conversi, saltem pro parte majori. Ipsi ergo sibi erant graviores tenebræ : id est, propria incredulitate ac obstinatione plus obtenebraverunt se intus, quam forinsecus obscurabantur; suisque sceleribus fuerunt sibi causa quod corruerunt in tenebras infernales, temporalibus illis tenebris graviores.
paras.en: [[17:20|But over them only was spread a heavy night|Solis autem illis superposita erat gravis nox]], lasting three days. Elsewhere day and night came in their usual course. [[17:20|an image of that darkness which was to come upon them|Imago tenebrarum, quæ superventura illis erat]]: that is, that night was a figure, an image and a sign of the darkness of hell, into which they were to go down after this life, because they were not converted, at least for the greater part. [[17:20|But they were to themselves more grievous than the darkness|Ipsi ergo sibi erant graviores tenebræ]] [Denis reads "graviores tenebræ", "a heavier darkness", where the Vulgate has "graviores tenebris", "more grievous than the darkness"]: that is, by their own unbelief and obstinacy they darkened themselves more within than they were darkened without; and by their crimes they were to themselves the cause of their falling into the darkness of hell, more grievous than that darkness of time.

18.title: DECLARATIO CAPITULI OCTAVIDECIMI : SANCTIS AUTEM TUIS MAXIMA ERAT LUX.
18.title_en: Declaration of the eighteenth chapter: But thy saints had a very great light

paras.t: Recitantur adhuc in isto capitulo effectus divinæ justitiæ circa Ægyptios, effectus quoque pietatis divinæ circa Hebræos.
paras.en: In this chapter are recounted still further the works of God's justice towards the Egyptians, and also the works of God's mercy towards the Hebrews.

paras.t: Sanctis autem tuis, scilicet filiis Israel, inter quos erant aliqui sancti et justi, aliorum comparatione perpauci, maxima erat lux : quia non solum illuminabantur forinsecus sole isto materiali, visibili, sed multo salubrius intus, Sole sapientiæ : de quo supra dixerunt iniqui, Sol intelligentiæ non est ortus nobis. Quamvis autem sol materialis non luxit eis splendidius quam aliis gentibus, tamen dicitur eis maxima lux fuisse, juxta consuetudinem Scripturarum, in quibus luminaria cœli dicuntur obscurari, dum homines quibus lucent incidunt in magna adversa, et clarius relucere, dum homines prosperantur.
paras.en: [[18:1|But thy saints|Sanctis autem tuis]], that is, the children of Israel, among whom there were some holy and just men, very few in comparison with the rest, [[18:1|had a very great light|maxima erat lux]]: for they were enlightened not only outwardly by this material, visible sun, but far more wholesomely within, by the Sun of wisdom, of which the wicked said above, [[Wis 5:6|the sun of understanding hath not risen upon us|Sol intelligentiæ non est ortus nobis]]. And although the material sun did not shine on them more brightly than on other nations, yet they are said to have had a very great light, after the custom of the Scriptures, in which the lights of heaven are said to be darkened when the men on whom they shine fall into great adversity[[Ezech 32:7||]][[Ezech 32:8||]], and to shine more brightly when men prosper[[Is 30:26||]].

paras.t: Et horum quidem, scilicet Hebræorum, vocem audiebant Ægyptii eis viciniores, quia Hebræi alta voce Deum laudabant ; sed figuram, id est personas et præsentialem lineamentorum corporum eorumdem imaginem, non videbant Ægyptii in præfatis tenebris triduo constituti. Et quia non et ipsi eadem passi sunt, id est, ex quo Hebræi non sunt puniti per easdem plagas, per quas Ægyptii puniebantur, magnificabant, id est, magnifice laudabant, te, Domine ; et qui ante læsi erant, id est Hebræi ab Ægyptiis multipliciter injuriati atque afflicti in rebus, personis, atque infantulis suis, quia non lædebantur plagis Ægyptiorum, gratias tibi agebant ; et ut esset differentia inter eos et Ægyptios, te Deum petebant, id est, te verum Deum invocabant, Ægyptii vero deos suos.
paras.en: [[18:1|and they heard their voice indeed|Et horum quidem]], that is, the voice of the Hebrews: the Egyptians who were nearer to them heard it, because the Hebrews were praising God with a loud voice; [[18:1|but did not see their shape|sed figuram]], that is, their persons and the present likeness of the features of their bodies: these the Egyptians, held for three days in the aforesaid darkness, did not see. [[18:1|And because they also did not suffer the same things|Et quia non et ipsi eadem passi sunt]], that is, since the Hebrews were not punished by the same plagues by which the Egyptians were punished, [[18:1|they glorified thee|magnificabant]], that is, they praised thee magnificently, O Lord; [[18:2|And they that before had been wronged|et qui ante læsi erant]], that is, the Hebrews, who had been injured by the Egyptians in many ways and afflicted in their goods, their persons and their little children, [[18:2|because they were not hurt now|quia non lædebantur]] by the plagues of the Egyptians, [[18:2|gave thanks|gratias tibi agebant]] to thee; and [[18:2|that there might be a difference|ut esset differentia]] between them and the Egyptians, they [[18:2|asked|petebant]] thee, God [Denis reads *te Deum petebant*, "they asked thee, God", where the Vulgate has *donum petebant*, "they asked a gift"], that is, they called upon thee, the true God, while the Egyptians called upon their gods.

paras.t: Propter quod ignis ardentem columnam ducem habuerunt ignotæ viæ : id est, dedisti eis columnam ignis, quæ eos præcessit in aere, mota ab angelo, et viam quam ante non ambulaverant, ipsis monstravit ; et solem sine læsura boni hospitii præstitisti, id est, contulisti eis in die ducatum solis sine læsura, per columnam nubis, quæ in die viam monstravit, et contra solis ardorem ac læsionem super Hebræos obumbravit, refrigerium eis præstans : solem, inquam, boni hospitii, quia duxit ad bonum hospitium aerem illustrando. Non quod filii Israel hospitabantur in via illa in domibus aliorum ; sed in propriis tentoriis papilionibusque manserunt, ubi nubes quievit : quoniam juxta motum et quietem nubis, procedebant et quiescebant, prout omnia ista in Exodo per diversa narrantur capitula.
paras.en: [[18:3|Therefore they received a burning pillar of fire for a guide of the way which they knew not|Propter quod ignis ardentem columnam ducem habuerunt ignotæ viæ]]: that is, thou gavest them a pillar of fire, which went before them in the air[[Ex 13:21||]], moved by an angel[[Ex 14:19||]], and showed them a way which they had not walked before; [[18:3|and thou gavest them a harmless sun of a good entertainment|et solem sine læsura boni hospitii præstitisti]], that is, thou didst bestow on them by day the guidance of a sun without harm, through the pillar of cloud, which by day showed the way[[Ex 13:21||]] and overshadowed the Hebrews against the heat and the harm of the sun, giving them refreshment: a sun, I say, *of a good entertainment* [*boni hospitii*, literally "of good lodging"], because by lighting up the air it led them to good lodging. Not that the children of Israel were lodged in the houses of others on that journey; but they stayed in their own tents and pavilions where the cloud rested: for according as the cloud moved or rested, they went forward or rested[[Ex 40:34||]][[Num 9:17||]], as all these things are told in various chapters of Exodus.

paras.t: Digni quidem illi, puta Ægyptii, carere luce solis, qua caruerunt in triduo illo ; interiori quoque illuminatione Solis justitiæ. Imo iniqui omnibus Dei beneficiis sunt indigni, et pane quo vescuntur, et aere quem respirant, et terra quam calcant. Et pati carcerem tenebrarum, id est aerem illum tenebrosissimum, quo tanquam in carcere tenebantur, non valentes se movere de loco ; qui inclusos custodiebant filios tuos, id est, filios Israel diu tenuerunt in terra sua sic coarctatos, quod eam egredi non valebant, per quos incipiebat incorruptum legis lumen sæculis dari, id est splendor et veritas legis Mosaicæ, quæ data est a Deo in monte Sinai, et quinquagesimo die post exitum de Ægypto cœpta est dari : imo in Ægypto, quando Deus præcepit Moysi qualiter doceret filios Israel ritum celebrandi manducandique pascha, et qualiter sanctificaret Deo omne primogenitum filiorum Israel, peccorumque eorum, prout in Exodo legitur.
paras.en: [[18:4|The others indeed were worthy|Digni quidem illi]], namely the Egyptians, [[18:4|to be deprived of light|carere luce]] of the sun, of which they were deprived for those three days; and of the inward enlightenment of the Sun of justice as well. Indeed the wicked are unworthy of all God's benefits, of the bread they eat, the air they breathe and the earth they tread. [[18:4|and imprisoned in darkness|Et pati carcerem tenebrarum]], that is, in that utterly dark air, in which they were held as in a prison, unable to move from their place; [[18:4|who kept thy children shut up|qui inclusos custodiebant filios tuos]], that is, who for a long time held the children of Israel so hemmed in within their land that they could not go out of it, [[18:4|by whom the pure light of the law was to be given to the world|per quos incipiebat incorruptum legis lumen sæculis dari]] [literally "was beginning to be given to the ages"], that is, the splendour and truth of the law of Moses, which was given by God on Mount Sinai[[Ex 31:18||]], and began to be given on the fiftieth day after the going out of Egypt[[Ex 19:1||]]; nay rather, in Egypt, when God commanded Moses how he should teach the children of Israel the rite of celebrating and eating the pasch[[Ex 12:1||]][[Ex 12:43||]], and how he should sanctify to God every firstborn of the children of Israel and of their cattle[[Ex 13:2||]], as we read in Exodus.

paras.t: Quamvis autem lex Moysis primo data sit filiis Israel, consequenter tamen hoc factum est ad aliarum gentium illuminationem : quia et multi gentilium ante adventum Christi fuerunt ad eam conversi ; vel saltem unum verum Deum ex ea colere didicerunt : sicut et Ptolemæus rex, ad cujus instantiam translati sunt libri veteris Testamenti. Deinde per Christum et ejus Apostolos, libri legis ac Prophetarum ad totius mundi profectum deducti sunt.
paras.en: Now although the law of Moses was given first to the children of Israel, yet in consequence this was done for the enlightenment of the other nations too: for many of the gentiles were converted to it before the coming of Christ, or at least learned from it to worship the one true God, as did King Ptolemy, at whose instance the books of the Old Testament were translated. Then through Christ and his Apostles the books of the Law and the Prophets were brought forth for the profit of the whole world.

paras.t: Quum cogitarent Ægyptii, justorum, id est Hebræorum, occidere infantes, id est masculos infantulos submergere : quod non solum cogitaverunt ac decreverunt, sed et opere compleverunt ad tempus, ut legitur in Exodo ; et uno exposito filio, scilicet Moyse, qui fuit in fiscella positus in flumine, et liberato, id est sublato de aqua ad imperium filiæ Pharaonis, ut in Exodo describitur : quod factum est in translationem illorum, id est ad exstirpationem et mortem Ægyptiorum, qui per Moysen sunt vastati ; vel, In translationem, id est eductionem Hebræorum per Moysen ex Ægypto. Multitudinem filiorum abstulisti, id est, primogenitos Ægyptiorum occidisti, in pœnam crudelitatis eorum commissæ in Hebræorum infantulos, prout in Exodo recitatur ; et pariter illos perdidisti in aqua valida, id est, in mari Rubro submersisti Ægyptios.
paras.en: [[18:5|And whereas they thought|Quum cogitarent]], namely the Egyptians, [[18:5|to kill the babes|occidere infantes]] [[18:5|of the just|justorum]], that is, of the Hebrews; that is, to drown the male infants: which they not only thought of and decreed, but for a time carried out in deed, as we read in Exodus[[Ex 1:22||]]; [[18:5|one child being cast forth|et uno exposito filio]], namely Moses, who was put in a basket in the river[[Ex 2:2||]][[Ex 2:3||]], [[18:5|and saved|et liberato]], that is, taken up out of the water at the command of Pharao's daughter, as Exodus relates: which was done [[18:5|to reprove them|in translationem illorum]] [*in translationem*, literally "for their removal"; the Vulgate has *traductionem*], that is, for the rooting out and death of the Egyptians, who were laid waste through Moses; or, *in translationem*, that is, for the leading of the Hebrews out of Egypt by Moses. [[18:5|thou tookest away a multitude of their children|Multitudinem filiorum abstulisti]], that is, thou slewest the firstborn of the Egyptians[[Ex 12:29||]], in punishment for the cruelty they had practised on the infants of the Hebrews, as is told in Exodus; [[18:5|and destroyedst them altogether in a mighty water|et pariter illos perdidisti in aqua valida]], that is, thou drownedst the Egyptians in the Red Sea[[Ex 14:27||]][[Ex 14:28||]].

paras.t: Illa enim nox, in qua omne primogenitum Ægypti percussum est, ante est cognita a patribus nostris. Deus enim prædixit eam Moysi, et per Moysen prænuntiata est universo populo suo, ut in Exodo legitur. Ut vere scientes patres nostri quibus juramentis, id est promissionibus Dei juramento firmatis, crediderunt : nam, ut patet in Genesi, Deus frequenter promisit atque juravit sanctis patriarchis, Abrahæ, Isaac, Jacob, dare eorum posteritati terram promissionis ; animæquiores essent, id est, longanimius sustinerent dilationem impletionis promissionum illarum, placatioresque essent interim in adversis.
paras.en: [[18:6|For that night|Illa enim nox]], in which every firstborn of Egypt was struck, [[18:6|was known before by our fathers|ante est cognita a patribus nostris]]. For God foretold it to Moses, and through Moses it was announced beforehand to all his people, as we read in Exodus[[Ex 11:1||]][[Ex 12:1||]]. [[18:6|that assuredly knowing|Ut vere scientes]], our fathers, [[18:6|what oaths|quibus juramentis]], that is, to what promises of God confirmed by oath, [[18:6|they had trusted to|crediderunt]]: for, as is plain in Genesis, God often promised and swore to the holy patriarchs Abraham, Isaac and Jacob to give the land of promise to their posterity[[Gen 12:7||]][[Gen 26:3||]][[Gen 28:13||]] [the margin also gives Gen. xxvii, 8, which does not fit; perhaps Gen 22:16 is meant]; [[18:6|they might be of better courage|animæquiores essent]], that is, that they might bear more patiently the delay in the fulfilment of those promises, and be calmer meanwhile in adversity.

paras.t: Suscepta est autem a populo tuo sanitas quidem justorum, id est, a populo Israel gratanter acceptata est liberatio sui ipsorum, qua a plagis Ægyptiorum erepti sunt ; injustorum autem exterminatio, id est, etiam devastationem Ægyptiorum populus tuus gratanter accepit, gaudens zelo justitiæ de adversariorum suorum punitione : juxta quod scriptum est, Lætabitur justus quum viderit vindictam. Sicut enim lædisti adversarios nostros Ægyptios, sic et nos provocans ad amorem tuum, et ad gratiarum actionem, magnificasti per multa et magna beneficia atque miracula.
paras.en: [[18:7|So thy people received the salvation of the just|Suscepta est autem a populo tuo sanitas quidem justorum]], that is, the people of Israel gladly received their own deliverance, by which they were snatched from the plagues of the Egyptians; [[18:7|and destruction of the unjust|injustorum autem exterminatio]], that is, thy people gladly received the laying waste of the Egyptians too, rejoicing with zeal for justice at the punishment of their adversaries, according to what is written: [[Ps 57:11|The just shall rejoice when he shall see the revenge|Lætabitur justus quum viderit vindictam]]. [[18:8|For as thou didst punish the adversaries|Sicut enim lædisti adversarios]], our adversaries the Egyptians, [[18:8|so thou didst also encourage|sic et nos provocans]] us to thy love and to thanksgiving, and [[18:8|glorify us|magnificasti]] by many great benefits and miracles.

paras.t: Absconse enim sacrificabant justi pueri bonorum : id est, filii Israel posteri sanctorum Patriarcharum, occulte in Ægypto immolabant agnum paschalem, metu Ægyptiorum, ut Exodus refert ; et justitiæ legem, id est præceptum illud justum de agno paschali, unanimiter impleverunt. Postea quoque legem Moysis concorditer acceperunt, atque implere proposuerunt, dicentes Moysi : Loquere tu nobis, et audiemus ; et postea, Omnia quæ locutus est Dominus, faciemus, et erimus obedientes. Similiter bona et mala recepturos justos : id est, audientes quod justi interdum paterentur non solum prospera, sed item adversa, concorditer disposuerunt hoc acceptare ; Patri jam decantantes laudes, id est, Deo omnium creatori super hoc laudes et gratiarum actiones canentes : juxta illud Judith : Non ulciscamur nos pro his quæ patimur ; sed reputantes peccatis nostris hæc ipsa supplicia minora esse, flagella Domini, quasi servi qui corripimur, ad emendationem, et non ad perditionem nostram evenisse credamus.
paras.en: [[18:9|For the just children of good men were offering sacrifice secretly|Absconse enim sacrificabant justi pueri bonorum]]: that is, the children of Israel, descendants of the holy Patriarchs, were secretly sacrificing the paschal lamb in Egypt for fear of the Egyptians, as Exodus relates[[Ex 12:6||]]; [[18:9|and they unanimously ordered a law of justice|et justitiæ legem]], that is, they fulfilled with one mind that just precept about the paschal lamb. Afterwards too they received the law of Moses with one accord and resolved to fulfil it, saying to Moses: [[Ex 20:19|Speak thou to us, and we will hear|Loquere tu nobis, et audiemus]]; and afterwards, [[Ex 24:7|All things that the Lord hath spoken, we will do, we will be obedient|Omnia quæ locutus est Dominus, faciemus, et erimus obedientes]][[Ex 24:3||]]. [[18:9|that the just should receive both good and evil alike|Similiter bona et mala recepturos justos]]: that is, hearing that the just would sometimes suffer not only prosperity but also adversity, they resolved with one accord to accept this; [[18:9|singing now the praises of the fathers|Patri jam decantantes laudes]] [Denis reads *Patri*, "to the Father", for the Vulgate's *patrum*, "of the fathers"], that is, singing praises and thanksgiving for this to God, the Creator of all, according to that of Judith: [[Jdt 8:26|let us not revenge ourselves for these things which we suffer|Non ulciscamur nos pro his quæ patimur]]; [[Jdt 8:27|But esteeming these very punishments to be less than our sins deserve, let us believe that these scourges of the Lord, with which like servants we are chastised, have happened for our amendment, and not for our destruction|sed reputantes peccatis nostris hæc ipsa supplicia minora esse, flagella Domini, quasi servi qui corripimur, ad emendationem, et non ad perditionem nostram evenisse credamus]].

paras.t: Resonabat autem inconvenientis inimicorum vox, id est confusa et deordinata vociferatio Ægyptiorum, in suis plagis ululantium et insanientium ; et flebilis audiebatur planctus ploratorum infantium, id est Ægyptiorum, qui deplorabant primogenitos suos occisos. Verumtamen primogeniti sic occisi, non fuerunt omnes infantes, imo multi eorum fuerunt virilis ætatis. Vel sensus est, quod audiebatur flebilis seu miserabilis vox infantium ploratorum, id est frequenter plorantium : quia in plagis illis infantes et pueri Ægyptiorum assidue flebant.
paras.en: [[18:10|But on the other side there sounded an ill according cry of the enemies|Resonabat autem inconvenientis inimicorum vox]], that is, the confused and disordered clamour of the Egyptians, howling and raving in their plagues; [[18:10|and a lamentable mourning was heard for the children that were bewailed|et flebilis audiebatur planctus ploratorum infantium]], that is, of the Egyptians, who were lamenting their firstborn that had been slain[[Ex 12:30||]]. Yet the firstborn thus slain were not all infants; indeed many of them were of man's age. Or the sense is that there was heard the lamentable or piteous voice of the bewailing infants, that is, of infants weeping often: for in those plagues the infants and children of the Egyptians wept continually [Denis takes *ploratorum infantium* either as "the infants who were bewailed" or as "the wailing infants"].

paras.t: Simili autem pœna servus Ægyptius cum domino suo Ægyptio afflictus est : quoniam servi communicabant, dominis suis in vitiis contra filios Israel ; et popularis, id est vulgaris, homo cum rege Pharaone similia passus est.
paras.en: [[18:11|And the servant suffered the same punishment as the master|Simili autem pœna servus Ægyptius cum domino suo Ægyptio afflictus est]], the Egyptian servant with his Egyptian master: for the servants shared with their masters in their wickedness against the children of Israel; [[18:11|and a common man|et popularis]], that is, an ordinary man, [[18:11|suffered in like manner as the king|homo cum rege Pharaone similia passus est]], King Pharao.

paras.t: Similiter ergo omnes Ægyptii, nobiles et ignobiles, uno nomine mortis, id est violenta morte occisos, mortuos habebant innumerabiles : et sumitur hic, Omnes, collective, non distributive. Hinc legitur in Exodo : Factum est in noctis medio, percussit Dominus omne primogenitum in terra Ægypti, a primogenito Pharaonis, qui sedebat in solio ejus, usque ad primogenitum captivæ, quæ erat in carcere, et omne primogenitum jumentorum. Nec enim ad sepeliendum mortuos vivi sufficiebant : siquidem in tota Ægypto non erat domus in qua non erat mortuus ; quoniam uno momento, id est improvise ac subito, quæ erat præclarior natio eorum, exterminata est, id est, nobiliores Ægyptiorum simul cum rege suo in mari Rubro submersi sunt.
paras.en: [[18:12|So all alike|Similiter ergo omnes]], all the Egyptians, noble and base, [[18:12|with one kind of death|uno nomine mortis]] [literally "by one name of death"], that is, slain by a violent death, [[18:12|had innumerable dead|mortuos habebant innumerabiles]]: and *all* is taken here collectively, not distributively [that is, of the Egyptians as a whole, not of each one of them]. Hence we read in Exodus: [[Ex 12:29|And it came to pass at midnight, the Lord slew every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharao, who sat on his throne, unto the firstborn of the captive woman that was in the prison, and all the firstborn of cattle|Factum est in noctis medio, percussit Dominus omne primogenitum in terra Ægypti, a primogenito Pharaonis, qui sedebat in solio ejus, usque ad primogenitum captivæ, quæ erat in carcere, et omne primogenitum jumentorum]]. [[18:12|Neither were the living sufficient to bury them|Nec enim ad sepeliendum mortuos vivi sufficiebant]], since in all Egypt [[Ex 12:30|there was not a house wherein there lay not one dead|non erat domus in qua non erat mortuus]]; [[18:12|for in one moment|quoniam uno momento]], that is, unforeseen and suddenly, [[18:12|the noblest offspring of them was destroyed|quæ erat præclarior natio eorum, exterminata est]], that is, the nobler of the Egyptians were drowned together with their king in the Red Sea[[Ex 15:4||]].

paras.t: De omnibus enim Ægyptiis non credentes Deo vero ac Moysi, propter beneficia, quæ Deus impendit Ægyptiis, liberando eos frequenter a plagis inflictis : post quarum cessationem manserunt in suis duritiis ; tunc quum primum fuit exterminium, id est interfectio, primogenitorum, sponderunt populum Dei se esse, id est, ex magna formidine cœperunt se Deo subjicere, et ejus omnipotentiam confiteri, ejusque gratiam implorare. Tunc enim Pharao dixit ad Moysen et Aaron : Abeuntes benedicite mihi. Urgebantque Ægyptii egredi populum Dei, dicentes : Omnes moriemur. Unde legitur Dominus prædixisse ad Moysen de Pharaone : Descendent omnes servi tui isti ad me, et adorabunt me, dicentes : Egredere tu, et omnis populus qui subjectus est tibi.
paras.en: [[18:13|For whereas they would not believe any thing|De omnibus enim Ægyptiis non credentes]], the Egyptians, in the true God and in Moses, [[18:13|by reason of the enchantments|propter beneficia]] [Denis reads *beneficia*, "benefits", where the Vulgate has *veneficia*, "enchantments"], that is, the benefits which God bestowed on the Egyptians by often delivering them from the plagues inflicted on them[[Ex 8:13||]][[Ex 9:33||]][[Ex 10:19||]], after whose ceasing they remained in their hardness[[Ex 8:15||]][[Ex 8:32||]][[Ex 9:35||]][[Ex 10:20||]]; [[18:13|then first upon the destruction|tunc quum primum fuit exterminium]], that is, the slaying, [[18:13|of the firstborn, they acknowledged the people to be of God|primogenitorum, sponderunt populum Dei se esse]] [Denis's text reads *se esse*, "that they themselves were the people of God"], that is, out of great fear they began to submit themselves to God, to confess his almighty power and to implore his favour. For then Pharao said to Moses and Aaron: [[Ex 12:32|departing bless me|Abeuntes benedicite mihi]]. And the Egyptians pressed the people of God to go forth, saying: [[Ex 12:33|We shall all die|Omnes moriemur]]. Hence we read that the Lord foretold to Moses concerning Pharao: [[Ex 11:8|And all these thy servants shall come down to me, and shall worship me, saying: Go forth thou, and all the people that is under thee|Descendent omnes servi tui isti ad me, et adorabunt me, dicentes : Egredere tu, et omnis populus qui subjectus est tibi]].

paras.t: Dum enim medium silentium contineret omnia, id est, cuncta ista inferiora in nocturno essent silentio : quod medium fuit inter exordium et terminum noctis ; et nox in suo cursu medium iter haberet, id est, in medio esset suæ durationis, consistentis in continuo fluxu, quum sit de numero successivorum. Unde jam allegatum est : Factum est autem in noctis medio, percussit Dominus omne primogenitum.
paras.en: [[18:14|For while all things were in quiet silence|Dum enim medium silentium contineret omnia]] [Denis reads *medium silentium*, "the midst of silence", as in the Introit, where the Vulgate has *quietum silentium*], that is, while all these lower things were in the silence of night, which was midway between the beginning and the end of the night; [[18:14|and the night was in the midst of her course|et nox in suo cursu medium iter haberet]], that is, was in the middle of its duration, which consists in continual flowing, since night is one of the things that are successive [that is, things whose being consists in passing, part after part, like time and motion]. Hence the words already alleged: [[Ex 12:29|And it came to pass at midnight, the Lord slew every firstborn|Factum est autem in noctis medio, percussit Dominus omne primogenitum]].

paras.t: Omnipotens sermo tuus, id est unigenitus Filius tuus, Verbum æternum, cujus oculis omnia nuda sunt et aperta : de quo ait Propheta, Verbo Domini cœli firmati sunt ; et Deus Pater, Eructavit cor meum verbum bonum ; Domine, exsiliens de cœlo, a regalibus sedibus, id est cœlestibus thronis, venit ; durus, id est rigorosus et justus, debellator Ægyptiorum, in mediam exterminii terram prosiluit, id est, a summo cœlo in omnem terram Ægypti descendit, et quasi saliens celerrime venit, non locum mutando, sed per angelum suæ justitiæ rigorem in Ægyptios exercendo. Aliqui vero per omnipotentem Dei sermonem, intelligunt jussionem Dei de occisione Ægyptiorum.
paras.en: [[18:15|Thy Almighty word|Omnipotens sermo tuus]], that is, thy only-begotten Son, the eternal Word, to whose eyes [[Heb 4:13|all things are naked and open|omnia nuda sunt et aperta]]; of whom the Prophet says, [[Ps 32:6|By the word of the Lord the heavens were established|Verbo Domini cœli firmati sunt]]; and God the Father, [[Ps 44:2|My heart hath uttered a good word|Eructavit cor meum verbum bonum]]; O Lord, [[18:15|leaped down from heaven from thy royal throne|exsiliens de cœlo, a regalibus sedibus]], that is, from the heavenly thrones, he came; [[18:15|fierce|durus]], that is, severe and just, [[18:15|conqueror|debellator]] of the Egyptians, [[18:15|into the midst of the land of destruction|in mediam exterminii terram prosiluit]] he leaped, that is, he came down from the height of heaven into all the land of Egypt, and came most swiftly, as if leaping, not by changing place, but by exercising the rigour of his justice on the Egyptians through an angel. Some, however, understand by the almighty word of God God's command for the slaying of the Egyptians.

paras.t: Gladius acutus, id est similis ensi omnia incidenti : quia cuncta quæ tetigit, interfecit. Nam et de increato Dei Patris sermone ait Apostolus, quod penetrabilior sit omni gladio anceps. Insimulatum, id est verum, non fictum, imperium tuum de Ægyptiorum interitu portans, id est, secum ferens et exsequens ; et stans per effectum suæ justitiæ, replevit omnia, id est quædam de omnibus, morte : quia in qualibet domo Ægyptiorum occidit primogenitum unum, Deo sic providente quod in qualibet domo fuit primogenitus aliquis ; et usque ad cælum attingebat stans in terra. Constat quod increatus sermo Dei sit incircumscriptus, sicut et Pater, et omnia impleat. Angelus vero exsecutor attingebat usque ad cœlum aerium, et quousque se sua actio extendebat. Angeli enim dicuntur esse in loco definitive ; et sic in uno, quod non in alio, quoniam ubi operantur, ibi sunt.
paras.en: [[18:16|With a sharp sword|Gladius acutus]] [literally "a sharp sword"], that is, like a blade that cuts through everything, for all that it touched it slew. For the Apostle too says of the uncreated Word of God the Father that it is [[Heb 4:12|more piercing than any two edged sword|penetrabilior sit omni gladio anceps]]. [[18:16|unfeigned|Insimulatum]], that is, true, not feigned, thy [[18:16|commandment|imperium tuum]] for the destruction of the Egyptians, [[18:16|carrying|portans]], that is, bearing it with him and carrying it out; [[18:16|and he stood|et stans]] through the working of his justice [[18:16|and filled all things|replevit omnia]], that is, something of all, [[18:16|with death|morte]]: for in every house of the Egyptians he slew one firstborn, God so providing that in every house there was some firstborn[[Ex 12:30||]]; [[18:16|and standing on the earth, reached even to heaven|et usque ad cælum attingebat stans in terra]]. It is certain that the uncreated Word of God is uncircumscribed, as is the Father, and fills all things. But the angel who carried out the sentence reached up to the heaven of the air, as far as his action extended. For angels are said to be in a place definitively [that is, not by filling it with dimensions as a body does, but by being there and not elsewhere]; and so they are in one place in such a way as not to be in another, since where they work, there they are.

paras.t: Tunc continuo visus somniorum malorum turbaverunt illos, scilicet Ægyptios, tam in occisione primogenitorum, quam paulo ante : quæ visiones imaginariæ et horrendæ, erant præsagia occisionum mox futurarum, aut signa præsentium, et excitationes dormientium ad percipiendum mortem primogenitorum ; et timores supervenerunt insperati.
paras.en: [[18:17|Then suddenly visions of evil dreams troubled them|Tunc continuo visus somniorum malorum turbaverunt illos]], namely the Egyptians, both at the slaying of the firstborn and a little before it: these imaginary and dreadful visions were forebodings of the slaughter soon to come, or signs of what was happening, and rousings of the sleepers to perceive the death of the firstborn; [[18:17|and fears unlooked for came upon them|et timores supervenerunt insperati]].

paras.t: Et alius alibi projectus semivivus, id est medius mortuus : id est, alius hic, alius ibi impellebatur a plaga sibi inflicta, sive ab angelo percutiente ; propter quam moriebatur, causam demonstrabat mortis : id est, tam violenta, improvisa, atque horribili morte ostendebat, quod ob impietatem in infantes Hebræorum commissam (qui infantuli erant hinc inde in flumen projecti), taliter moriebatur.
paras.en: [[18:18|And one thrown here, another there, half dead|Et alius alibi projectus semivivus]], that is, half dead: that is, one here, another there, was flung down by the stroke laid on him, or by the angel who struck; [[18:18|shewed the cause of his death|propter quam moriebatur, causam demonstrabat mortis]] [literally "shewed the cause of death for which he was dying"], that is, by so violent, unforeseen and horrible a death he showed that it was for the wickedness committed against the infants of the Hebrews (who as little children had been thrown here and there into the river) that he was dying in this way.

paras.t: Visiones enim, quæ illos turbaverunt in somno, et immittebantur, ut creditur, ab angelis tenebrarum, juxta illud in Psalmo, Immissiones per angelos malos ; hæc præmonebant, id est, plagam hanc designabant, ut tactum est, ne Ægyptii nescii quare mala patiebantur, perirent, id est, æternaliter damnarentur, nescientes ob quam culpam suam, mala illa pœnalia sustinebant : per quæ Deus, quantum in se fuit, ex sua pietate immensa admonuit ipsos, ut per tormenta illa suas adverterent culpas, et pœnituerent, ac crederent, sicque per temporalia illa supplicia, evaderent sempiterna.
paras.en: [[18:19|For the visions that troubled them|Visiones enim, quæ illos turbaverunt]] in sleep, and were sent, as is believed, by the angels of darkness, according to that in the Psalm, [[Ps 77:49|which he sent by evil angels|Immissiones per angelos malos]] [literally "sendings in by evil angels"], [[18:19|foreshewed these things|hæc præmonebant]], that is, signified this plague, as was touched on above, [[18:19|lest they should perish, and not know why they suffered these evils|ne Ægyptii nescii quare mala patiebantur, perirent]], that is, lest the Egyptians should be damned eternally, not knowing for what fault of theirs they were bearing those penal evils: by which God, as far as lay in him, out of his boundless mercy warned them to recognise their faults through those torments, and to repent and believe, and so by those temporal punishments to escape the everlasting ones.

paras.t: Tetigit autem tunc : non quando filii Israel erant adhuc in Ægypto, sed diu post, quando fuerunt in deserto : quod totum tempus, fuit tempus perrectionis ad terram promissionis. Ideo sic exponendum est : Tunc, quando erant in via ad obtinendam terram eis promissam, tetigit et justos, scilicet filios Israel, inter quos fuerunt aliqui justi, tentatio mortis, id est murmuratio contra Moysen et Aaron, morte digna, ac morte punita. Quæ tentatio fuit ambitionis atque invidiæ : quoniam Core cum suis, Dathan quoque et Abiron et Hon invidebant principatui Moysis et pontificio Aaron, dicentes : Sufficiat vobis quod omnis multitudo sanctorum est, et in ipsis est Dominus : cur elevamini super populum Domini? prout Numerorum sextodecimo scriptum est. Et commotio in eremo facta est multitudinis, id est seditio multorum contra Moysen et Aaron : non solum ducentorum quinquaginta virorum, qui cum Core fuerunt, et thurificando combusti fuerunt ; sed et multorum millium, qui absorptis Dathan, Abiron et Core a terra, commoti sunt valde. Unde in Numeris legitur : Murmuravit autem omnis multitudo filiorum Israel sequenti die contra Moysen et Aaron, dicens : Vos interfecistis populum Domini. Sed non diu permansit ira tua, id est, pœna propter hoc scelus a Deo illis inflicta, cito sortita est finem.
paras.en: [[18:20|But the just also were afterwards touched|Tetigit autem tunc]] [literally "but then touched"]: *then*, not when the children of Israel were still in Egypt, but long afterwards, when they were in the desert; and that whole time was the time of the journey to the land of promise. So it must be explained thus: *then*, when they were on the way to obtaining the land promised them, there touched [[18:20|the just also|et justos]], namely the children of Israel, among whom there were some just, [[18:20|an assault of death|tentatio mortis]] [*tentatio mortis*, literally "a trial of death"], that is, murmuring against Moses and Aaron, deserving death and punished by death[[Num 16:1||]][[Num 16:12||]][[Num 16:41||]][[Num 16:31||]][[Num 16:35||]][[Num 16:47||]]. This trial was one of ambition and envy: for Core with his followers, and Dathan too and Abiron and Hon, envied Moses his rule and Aaron his high priesthood, saying: [[Num 16:3|Let it be enough for you, that all the multitude consisteth of holy ones, and the Lord is among them: Why lift you up yourselves above the people of the Lord?|Sufficiat vobis quod omnis multitudo sanctorum est, et in ipsis est Dominus : cur elevamini super populum Domini?]], as is written in the sixteenth chapter of Numbers. [[18:20|and there was a disturbance of the multitude in the wilderness|Et commotio in eremo facta est multitudinis]], that is, a sedition of many against Moses and Aaron: not only of the two hundred and fifty men who were with Core and were burnt while offering incense[[Num 16:2||]][[Num 16:35||]], but also of many thousands, who were greatly stirred up when Dathan, Abiron and Core had been swallowed by the earth. Hence we read in Numbers: [[Num 16:41|The following day all the multitude of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and Aaron, saying: You have killed the people of the Lord|Murmuravit autem omnis multitudo filiorum Israel sequenti die contra Moysen et Aaron, dicens : Vos interfecistis populum Domini]]. [[18:20|but thy wrath did not long continue|Sed non diu permansit ira tua]], that is, the punishment inflicted on them by God for this crime quickly came to an end.

paras.t: Properans enim homo sine querela, id est Aaron, pontifex justus, deprecari pro populis, qui murmuraverunt, atque incendio puniebantur, proferens servitutis suæ scutum, id est spiritualem armaturam sui pontificalis officii, utpote orationem : arma etenim sacerdotis, sunt orationes et lacrimæ, ut sanctus ait Ambrosius ; et per incensum deprecationem allegans, id est, thurificando exorans cum allegatione meritorum sanctorum Patriarcharum : quorum merita allegavit, ut oratio sua illorum meritis exaudibilior fieret. Allegans quoque (ut probabile est) promissiones divinitus factas Abrahæ, Isaac, et Jacob, pro posteris eorum, de introductione ipsorum in terram promissionis. Sic namque et Moyses allegans oravit, quando filii Israel aureum vitulum adoraverunt. Restitit iræ, id est punitioni murmuratorum, et finem imposuit necessitati, id est angustiæ mortis, quam multi tunc sustinuerunt ; ostendens quoniam tuus est famulus : per hoc namque quod tam ferventer oravit pro murmurantibus contra ipsum adversariis suis, et quod tam cito ac mirabiliter exaudiebatur a Domino, patuit quod vere esset minister placitus Deo, et pontifex dignus.
paras.en: [[18:21|For a blameless man made haste|Properans enim homo sine querela]], that is, Aaron, the just high priest, [[18:21|to pry for the people|deprecari pro populis]], who had murmured and were being punished by fire, [[18:21|bringing forth the shield of his ministry|proferens servitutis suæ scutum]], that is, the spiritual armour of his high-priestly office, namely [[18:21|prayer|orationem]]: for the arms of a priest are prayers and tears, as St Ambrose says; [[18:21|and by incense making supplication|et per incensum deprecationem allegans]] [*allegans*, "alleging", that is, pleading], that is, entreating by offering incense, while alleging the merits of the holy Patriarchs: whose merits he alleged so that his prayer might be the more readily heard through their merits. He alleged too (as is probable) the promises made by God to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob for their descendants, about bringing them into the land of promise. For so did Moses also pray, alleging them, when the children of Israel worshipped the golden calf[[Ex 32:13||]]. [[18:21|withstood the wrath|Restitit iræ]], that is, the punishment of the murmurers, [[18:21|and put an end to the calamity|et finem imposuit necessitati]], that is, to the distress of death which many were then suffering; [[18:21|shewing that he was thy servant|ostendens quoniam tuus est famulus]]: for by praying so fervently for his adversaries who murmured against him, and by being heard by the Lord so quickly and so wonderfully, it was made plain that he was truly a minister pleasing to God and a worthy high priest.

paras.t: Denique ad intelligendum hæc, recurrendum esset ad historiam libri Numerorum : in qua inter cetera legitur, quod quum Moyses et Aaron ad tabernaculum confugissent, et Dominus vellet universam illam murmuratorum multitudinem repente occidere, Moyses dixit ad Aaron : Tolle thuribulum, et hausto igne de altari, mitte incensum desuper, pergens cito ad populum, ut ores pro eis : jam enim egressa est ira a Domino, et plaga desævit. Quod quum fecisset Aaron, et cucurrisset ad mediam multitudinem, quam jam vastabat incendium, obtulit thymiama ; et stans inter mortuos ac viventes, pro populo deprecatus est, et plaga cessavit. Et percussa sunt quatuordecim millia hominum.
paras.en: Finally, to understand these things one would have to go back to the history in the book of Numbers, where among other things we read that when Moses and Aaron had fled to the tabernacle, and the Lord wished to slay that whole multitude of murmurers at once[[Num 16:43||]], Moses said to Aaron: [[Num 16:46|Take the censer, and putting fire in it from the altar, put incense upon it, and go quickly to the people to pray for them: for already wrath is gone out from the Lord, and the plague rageth|Tolle thuribulum, et hausto igne de altari, mitte incensum desuper, pergens cito ad populum, ut ores pro eis : jam enim egressa est ira a Domino, et plaga desævit]]. [[Num 16:47|When Aaron had done this, and had run to the midst of the multitude which the burning fire was now destroying, he offered the incense|Quod quum fecisset Aaron, et cucurrisset ad mediam multitudinem, quam jam vastabat incendium, obtulit thymiama]]: [[Num 16:48|And standing between the dead and the living, he prayed for the people, and the plague ceased|et stans inter mortuos ac viventes, pro populo deprecatus est, et plaga cessavit]]. And fourteen thousand men were struck[[Num 16:49||]].

paras.t: Vicit autem turbas, id est improbitatem tribuum Israel, et prætactam eorum plagam exstinxit, non virtute corporis, nec armatura potentiæ, id est non corporali fortitudine, nec armorum potentia ; sed verbo illum, qui se vexabat, subjecit, id est, oratione sua exstinxit ignem, qui plebem illam incenderat, et ex consequenti vexavit et ipsum Aaron illis compassionem. Vel per vexatorem illum, intelligitur spiritus, cujus ministerio incendium infligebatur. Juramenta patrum et testamentum confirmans, id est, in sua oratione recolens et allegans, qualiter Deus cum jurejurando sanctis promiserat Patriarchis semini eorum dare terram promissionis, et qualiter testamentum iniit cum eisdem, et cum filiis Israel, in monte Sinai, quando et Moyses dixit : Hic est sanguis testamenti quod mandavit ad vos Deus. Vel sensus est, quod ipse Aaron Deum placando, impetravit firmam impletionem promissionum Dei factarum plebi præfatæ.
paras.en: [[18:22|And he overcame the disturbance|Vicit autem turbas]] [*turbas*, literally "the crowds"], that is, the wickedness of the tribes of Israel, and quenched the plague on them already mentioned, [[18:22|not by strength of body nor with force of arms|non virtute corporis, nec armatura potentiæ]], that is, not by bodily strength nor by the might of weapons; [[18:22|but with a word he subdued him that punished them|sed verbo illum, qui se vexabat, subjecit]] [literally "him who was troubling him"], that is, by his prayer he put out the fire which had burnt that people, and which in consequence had troubled Aaron himself as well, through his compassion for them. Or by the one who troubled is understood the spirit by whose ministry the burning was inflicted. [[18:22|alleging the oath and covenant made with the fathers|Juramenta patrum et testamentum confirmans]] [Denis reads *confirmans*, "confirming", where the Vulgate has *commemorans*], that is, recalling and alleging in his prayer how God had promised with an oath to the holy Patriarchs to give the land of promise to their seed, and how he made a covenant with them and with the children of Israel on Mount Sinai, when Moses also said: [[Ex 24:8|This is the blood of the covenant|Hic est sanguis testamenti]] which God hath enjoined unto you [Denis's wording, *quod mandavit ad vos Deus*, is that of Heb 9:20, which quotes this verse]. Or the sense is that Aaron himself, by appeasing God, obtained the firm fulfilment of the promises God had made to that people.

paras.t: Quum enim jam acervatim cecidissent super alterutrum mortui, id est, quum in præfato incendio, in quo tot millia sunt combusta, unus super alterum, et hi super illos, cum cumulis corruissent : quia ex vehementia pœnæ agitabantur hinc inde, et unus alium impulit ac prostravit ; interstitit, id est, Aaron in medio stetit inter adhuc viventes, ac mortuos, et amputavit, id est, cessare fecit, impetum incendii, quod morabatur ad residuos. Unde subjungitur, et divisit illam quæ ad vivos ducebat viam, id est, transitum ignis properantis ad viventes, impedivit ac repulit.
paras.en: [[18:23|For when they were now fallen down dead by heaps one upon another|Quum enim jam acervatim cecidissent super alterutrum mortui]], that is, when in the aforesaid burning, in which so many thousands were consumed, one had fallen upon another and these upon those, in heaps: for in the violence of the punishment they were driven this way and that, and one pushed another and threw him down; [[18:23|he stood between|interstitit]], that is, Aaron stood in the midst between those still living and the dead, [[18:23|and stayed|et amputavit]] [literally "cut off"], that is, made to cease, [[18:23|the assault|impetum]] of the fire, which was lingering on toward those who remained. Hence it is added, [[18:23|and cut off the way to the living|et divisit illam quæ ad vivos ducebat viam]], that is, he hindered and drove back the passage of the fire hastening towards the living.

paras.t: Denique ad tantam efficaciam orationis Aaron contulit et dignitas sui officii, qua erat vicarius Dei et representativus ipsius : ad cujus officii commendationem Deus multa fecit per Aaron. Ideo subditur : In veste enim poderis quam habebat, totus erat orbis terrarum.
paras.en: Furthermore, the dignity of his office also contributed to so great an efficacy in Aaron's prayer, by which he was God's vicar and represented him; and to commend that office God did many things through Aaron. Therefore it is added: [[18:24|For in the priestly robe which he wore, was the whole world|In veste enim poderis quam habebat, totus erat orbis terrarum]] [*vestis poderis*, "the robe reaching to the feet"].

paras.t: Poderis dicitur vestis hyacinthina, seu linea, corpori sacerdotis adstricta, usque ad pedes ejus descendens. Porro, per orbem terrarum, intelligitur hic non solum terræ elementum, sed et sphæra aliorum elementorum ; et per vestem poderis, accipitur congeries quædam sacerdotalium seu pontificalium vestimentorum. Itaque in ornamentis seu vestibus pontificis representative fuit mundus iste sensibilis : ad designandum quod pontifex fuit minister atque vicarius Creatoris ac Domini universorum. Feminalia etenim linea et tunica stricta, representabant terram, quia ex terra nascitur linum ; circumvolutio baltei, Oceanum, qui ambit et cingit terram. Tunica hyacinthina per suum colorem significavit aerem : per cujus tintinnabula figurabantur tonitrua ; et per mala granata, quæ igni sunt coloris, coruscationes. Per superhumerale multiplici varietate ornatum, cœlum sidereum ; et per duos illius onychinos, duo hemisphæria, seu sol et luna. Per duodecim gemmas, duodecim signa zodiaci : quæ gemmæ positæ erant in rationali, ad innuendum quod in cœlestibus continentur rationes omnium terrenorum. Hinc medium ornamentum recte vocatum est rationale, quia rationibus cuncta sunt plena. Per cidarim significatum est cœlum empyreum ; per laminam auream nomine Dei inscriptam, ipse Deus gloriosus et adorandus, præsidens universis. — His concordat Hieronymus, dicens : Hebræi per byssum intelligunt terram ; per purpuram, mare, quia cochleis maris intingitur : per hyacinthum, aerem, atque per coccum, ignem.
paras.en: *Poderis* is the name of a violet or linen garment fitted close to the priest's body and reaching down to his feet. Further, by *the whole world* is understood here not only the element of earth but also the sphere of the other elements; and by *the robe reaching to the feet* is meant the whole set of the priestly or high-priestly vestments. So in the ornaments or vestments of the high priest this sensible world was represented, to signify that the high priest was the minister and vicar of the Creator and Lord of all things. For the linen breeches and the close-fitting tunic represented the earth, since flax grows from the earth; the winding of the girdle, the Ocean, which surrounds and girds the earth. The violet tunic by its colour signified the air, and by its little bells were figured the thunders, and by the pomegranates, which are the colour of fire, the lightnings. By the ephod [*superhumerale*], adorned with manifold variety, the starry heaven; and by its two onyx stones, the two hemispheres, or the sun and the moon. By the twelve gems, the twelve signs of the zodiac: and these gems were set in the rational [the breastplate, Latin *rationale*], to signify that in the heavenly bodies are contained the reasons of all earthly things. Hence the middle ornament was rightly called the *rational*, because all things are full of reasons [*rationes*, a play on *rationale*]. By the mitre the empyrean heaven was signified; by the golden plate inscribed with the name of God, God himself, glorious and adorable, presiding over all things. With this Jerome agrees, saying: The Hebrews understand by the fine linen the earth; by the purple, the sea, because it is dyed with the shellfish of the sea; by the violet, the air; and by the scarlet, fire.

paras.t: Et parentum magnalia, id est duodecim Patriarcharum nomina, in quatuor ordi[…] In rationali enim erant quatuor ordines gemmarum, distincti per ternarium, et in duodecim illis gemmis sculpta erant nomina duodecim Patriarcharum seu tribuum, in memoriam earum coram Deo. Hinc Dominus jussit : Pones in rationali quatuor ordines lapidum : in primo versu, id est ordine, erit sardius, topazius, et smaragdus ; in secundo, carbunculus, sapphirus, et jaspis ; in tertio, ligurius, achates, et amethystus ; in quarto, chrysolithus, onychinus, et beryllus. Inclusi auro erunt ; duodecim nominibus cælabuntur, singuli lapides nominibus singulorum per duodecim tribus. Et magnificentia tua in diademate capitis illius scripta erat : id est, sanctum, ineffabile, et proprium nomen tuum tetragrammaton, scriptum fuit in aurea lamina, diademati seu mitræ pontificali adjuncta.
paras.en: [[18:24|the glory of the fathers|Et parentum magnalia]] [literally "the great things of the fathers"], that is, the names of the twelve Patriarchs, [[18:24|in the four rows|in quatuor ordi]] […]. For in the rational there were four rows of gems, set in threes, and on those twelve gems were engraved the names of the twelve Patriarchs or tribes, as a memorial of them before God. Hence the Lord commanded: [[Ex 28:17|thou shalt set in it four rows of stones|Pones in rationali quatuor ordines lapidum]]: [[Ex 28:17|In the first row|in primo versu]], that is, rank [*versus*, a line or row], [[Ex 28:17|shall be a sardius stone, and a topaz, and an emerald|erit sardius, topazius, et smaragdus]]; [[Ex 28:18|In the second a carbuncle, a sapphire, and a jasper|in secundo, carbunculus, sapphirus, et jaspis]]; [[Ex 28:19|In the third a ligurius, an agate, and an amethyst|in tertio, ligurius, achates, et amethystus]]; [[Ex 28:20|In the fourth a chrysolite, an onyx, and a beryl. They shall be set in gold|in quarto, chrysolithus, onychinus, et beryllus. Inclusi auro erunt]]; [[Ex 28:21|with twelve names shall they be engraved, each stone with the name of one according to the twelve tribes|duodecim nominibus cælabuntur, singuli lapides nominibus singulorum per duodecim tribus]] [the margin gives Exod. xxxviii, 17-21; the passage is Exod 28:17-21]. [[18:24|and thy majesty was written upon the diadem of his head|Et magnificentia tua in diademate capitis illius scripta erat]]: that is, thy holy, ineffable and proper name, the tetragrammaton, was written on the golden plate joined to the diadem or high-priestly mitre[[Ex 28:36||]][[Ex 28:37||]][[Ex 28:38||]] [the margin gives Ibid. 36-38, that is, Exod 28:36-38].

paras.t: His autem ornamentis pontificalibus, ratione mysterii, cessit qui exterminabat, id est ignis qui filios Israel præfatos incendit, et hæc extimuit, id est, per modum timentis se habuit ignis ille, non procedendo contra hæc ad residuos vivos. Magis autem cessit, et timuit Deum in istis, juxta tropum quo inanimata et irrationalia dicuntur Deum timere, juxta illud in Psalmo : Mare vidit, et fugit. Vel per illum qui exterminavit, intelligitur spiritus cujus ministerio fiebat illa punitio. Erat enim sola tentatio iræ, id est, sola illa punitio seu vindicta divinæ justitiæ erat sufficiens ad exterminandum totaliter filios Israel, nisi sic ipse Aaron subvenisset. Vel : Sola tentatio, id est murmuratio filiorum Israel contra Moysen et Aaron, fuit sufficiens iræ, id est causa sufficiens, provocans iram seu ultionem Dei adversus illos iniquos ad delendum eos, nisi pontifex Deum placasset.
paras.en: [[18:25|And to these|His autem]] high-priestly ornaments, by reason of the mystery, [[18:25|the destroyer gave place|cessit qui exterminabat]], that is, the fire which burned the aforesaid children of Israel, [[18:25|and was afraid of them|et hæc extimuit]], that is, that fire behaved like one afraid, not advancing past these to those still living. But rather it gave way to God and feared God in these things, by the figure of speech in which lifeless and irrational things are said to fear God, as in that of the Psalm: [[Ps 113:3|The sea saw and fled|Mare vidit, et fugit]]. Or by him who destroyed is understood the spirit by whose ministry that punishment was carried out. [[18:25|for the proof only of wrath|Erat enim sola tentatio iræ]], that is, that punishment or vengeance of God's justice alone [[18:25|was enough|sufficiens]] to destroy the children of Israel utterly, had not Aaron himself thus come to their help. Or: *the trial only*, that is, the murmuring of the children of Israel against Moses and Aaron, *was enough for wrath*, that is, a sufficient cause, provoking the wrath or vengeance of God against those wicked men to blot them out, had not the high priest appeased God [*tentatio*, "trial" or "testing", the word the Douay-Rheims renders "proof" here and "assault" in v. 20].

paras.t: Denique de significatione et mysticis rationibus sacerdotalium vestium et pontificalium ornamentorum, atque gemmarum et sculpturæ earum, super Exodum dictum est plenius, secundum Josephum, Hieronymum, Bedam, aliosque doctores.
paras.en: Lastly, of the meaning and the mystical reasons of the priestly vestments and the high-priestly ornaments, and of the gems and their engraving, more has been said on Exodus, following Josephus, Jerome, Bede and other doctors [the margin refers to the commentary on Exodus, Art. LV and LVI].

paras.t: Insuper, quæ in isto capitulo dicta sunt de Hebræis atque Ægyptiis, facile esset applicare Christianis, et eorum persecutoribus perfidis ac injustis : quibus sævientibus contra Christifideles, ipsis veraciter Christianis maxima lux est, impiis densissime excæcatis, eo quod populum Christi coarctent et vexent.
paras.en: Moreover, what is said in this chapter of the Hebrews and the Egyptians could easily be applied to Christians and to their faithless and unjust persecutors: while these rage against the faithful of Christ, those who are truly Christians have a very great light, and the wicked are most thickly blinded, because they hem in and harass the people of Christ.

paras.t: Quod vero dictum est, Dum medium silentium teneret omnia, exponi potest de primo Christi adventu : qui a summo cœlo de sinu Patris venit per Incarnationis mysterium in uterum Virginis, dum medium silentium teneret omnia, id est, nullus præsumere posset de meritis suis, et vix aliquis diabolo resisteret, et nox, id est umbra legis, statusque veteris Testamenti obscurus ac typicus, in suo cursu medium iter haberet, id est, adhuc duraret. Unde postea dixit Apostolus : Nox præcessit. Qui sermo increatus, fuit durus debellator invisibilium hostium ; venit in mediam exterminii terram, id est in Judæam, cujus habitatores fuerunt ab æriis potestatibus spiritualiter victi, et exterminati pro maxima parte ; portans Patris imperium, tanquam magni consilii Angelus, dicens : Sicut mandatum dedit mihi Pater, sic facio. Replevitque omnia morte, invisibiles adversarios deprimendo, et suos salubriter mortificando, vitia occidendo, reprobos quoque Judæos derelinquendo. Propter quod dixit : In judicium ego veni in hunc mundum : ut qui non vident, videant ; et qui vident, cæci fiant. Positus enim fuit in ruinam et resurrectionem multorum in Israel, et in signum cui contradiceretur. Et ipsemet dixit : Non veni pacem mittere in terram, sed gladium. Atque, ut in prima S. Joannis habetur Canonica, In hoc apparuit Filius Dei, ut dissolvat opera diaboli.
paras.en: As for the words, [[18:14|while all things were in quiet silence|Dum medium silentium teneret omnia]], they can be expounded of the first coming of Christ, who came from the height of heaven, from the bosom of the Father, through the mystery of the Incarnation into the womb of the Virgin, *while the midst of silence held all things*: that is, when no one could presume on his own merits, and scarcely anyone resisted the devil; [[18:14|and the night|et nox]], that is, the shadow of the Law and the dark and figurative state of the Old Testament, [[18:14|was in the midst of her course|in suo cursu medium iter haberet]], that is, still lasted. Hence the Apostle said afterwards: [[Rom 13:12|The night is passed|Nox præcessit]]. This uncreated Word was [[18:15|a fierce conqueror|durus debellator]] of the invisible enemies; he came [[18:15|into the midst of the land of destruction|in mediam exterminii terram]], that is, into Judea, whose inhabitants had been spiritually conquered by the powers of the air and destroyed for the most part; [[18:16|carrying|portans]] the Father's command, as the Angel of great counsel [*magni consilii Angelus*, the title given to Christ in the Introit of the third Mass of Christmas, from Is 9:6 in the Septuagint], saying: [[John 14:31|as the Father hath given me commandments, so do I|Sicut mandatum dedit mihi Pater, sic facio]]. and he [[18:16|filled all things with death|Replevitque omnia morte]], by casting down the invisible adversaries, by mortifying his own unto salvation, by slaying vices, and by forsaking the reprobate Jews too. Wherefore he said: [[John 9:39|For judgment I am come into this world: that they who see not may see; and they who see may become blind|In judicium ego veni in hunc mundum : ut qui non vident, videant ; et qui vident, cæci fiant]]. For he was [[Luke 2:34|set for the fall and for the resurrection of many in Israel and for a sign which shall be contradicted|in ruinam et resurrectionem multorum in Israel, et in signum cui contradiceretur]]. And he himself said: [[Matt 10:34|I came not to send peace, but the sword|Non veni pacem mittere in terram, sed gladium]]. And, as we have it in the first canonical Epistle of St John, [[1 John 3:8|For this purpose the Son of God appeared, that he might destroy the works of the devil|In hoc apparuit Filius Dei, ut dissolvat opera diaboli]] [the margin gives Joann. iii, 8; the verse is 1 John 3:8].

paras.t: Postremo quæritur circa præhabita, utrum interfectio primogenitorum Ægypti facta sit ministerio angeli boni, aut potius angeli mali. Et videtur quod ministerio angeli sancti : quia manifeste hic dicitur, quod omnipotens sermo Dei, exsiliens et stans in terra, replevit omnia morte. Glossa quoque circa hoc ait, quod ministerio angeli fecit judicia in primogenitis Ægyptiorum : et hoc multi doctores tanquam probabilius tenent. Augustinus vero in expositione psalmi septuagesimi septimi, super illud, Misit Dominus in eos iram indignationis suæ, manifeste testatur quod per angelum malum facta sit percussio primogenitorum illorum. De hac quæstione super Exodum in expositione duodecimi capituli diffusius scripsi : et propter diversa motiva ibidem inducta, tanquam probabilius tenui quod sicut sub Ezechia rege percussi sunt Assyrii ab angelo sancto, similiter Sodomitæ per sanctos angelos subversi sunt ; ita et primogenita Ægypti. Nec videtur ratio cur plaga illa potius per angelum tenebrarum inflicta sit, quam aliæ plagæ Ægyptiis tunc illatæ : de quibus Augustinus non audet dicere quod per angelos malos illatæ sint. Hæc pro nunc sufficiat tetigisse, quæ prætacto loco exquisitius sunt inducta.
paras.en: Lastly, it is asked about what has gone before whether the slaying of the firstborn of Egypt was done by the ministry of a good angel or rather of a bad one. And it seems that it was by the ministry of a holy angel, since it is plainly said here that the almighty Word of God, [[18:15|leaped down|exsiliens]] and [[18:16|standing on the earth|stans in terra]], [[18:16|filled all things with death|replevit omnia morte]]. The Gloss too says on this that he did judgment on the firstborn of the Egyptians by the ministry of an angel; and many doctors hold this as the more probable. But Augustine, in his exposition of the seventy-seventh Psalm, on the words [[Ps 77:49|And he sent upon them the wrath of his indignation|Misit Dominus in eos iram indignationis suæ]], plainly testifies that the striking of those firstborn was done by a bad angel. I have written on this question at greater length on Exodus, in the exposition of the twelfth chapter [the margin refers to the commentary on Exodus, Art. XXI]; and for the various reasons brought forward there I held it as more probable that, as the Assyrians were struck by a holy angel under King Ezechias[[4 Kings 19:35||]], and as the Sodomites were overthrown by holy angels[[Gen 19:1||]][[Gen 19:13||]], so also were the firstborn of Egypt. Nor does there seem to be any reason why that plague should have been inflicted by an angel of darkness rather than the other plagues then brought on the Egyptians, of which Augustine does not venture to say that they were brought by bad angels. Let it suffice for now to have touched on these things, which are set out more carefully in the place mentioned.

paras.t: Quod vero allegatur ex Psalmo, Immissiones per angelos malos, super Exodum est solutum, intelligendo per immissiones, inspirationes pravissimas, quas immittentibus angelis malis, conceperunt Ægyptii contra Hebræos. Et sicut ex dictis in isto capitulo constat, possunt per illas immissiones intelligi visiones illæ horrendæ ac turbativæ turbulentorum phantasmatum, quas in somno sustinuerunt Ægyptii.
paras.en: As for what is alleged from the Psalm, [[Ps 77:49|which he sent by evil angels|Immissiones per angelos malos]], this was answered on Exodus, by understanding by *sendings* the most wicked inspirations which the Egyptians conceived against the Hebrews at the prompting of bad angels. And, as is clear from what is said in this chapter, those *sendings* can be understood of the dreadful and troubling [[18:19|visions|visiones]] of turbulent phantasms which the Egyptians endured in sleep.

paras.t: Amplius, quamvis hic liber non sit in canone, tamen argumentum ex eo sumptum hoc loco, videtur sufficere apud Catholicos : quia de veritate libri hujus non dubitat mater Ecclesia, præsertim quantum ad verba nunc allegata, videlicet, Dum medium silentium teneret omnia : quæ in officio Missæ pro introitu sunt assumpta, quamvis quoad mysticum sensum præcipue, quem tamen in litteræ veritate fundari oportet.
paras.en: Further, although this book is not in the canon [Denis follows the opinion, common before the Council of Trent, that Wisdom was not in the canon of the Hebrews], yet an argument taken from it in this place seems to suffice among Catholics: for Mother Church does not doubt the truth of this book, especially as regards the words just alleged, namely, [[18:14|while all things were in quiet silence|Dum medium silentium teneret omnia]], which are taken up in the office of the Mass for the Introit [of the Sunday within the octave of Christmas], though chiefly as regards the mystical sense; and yet that sense must be grounded in the truth of the letter.

19.title: EXPOSITIO CAPITULI NONIDECIMI ET ULTIMI : IMPIIS AUTEM USQUE IN NOVISSIMUM, ETC.
19.title_en: Exposition of the nineteenth and last chapter: But as to the wicked, even to the end, etc.

paras.t: […] que Hebræorum, hic agitur.
paras.en: […] of the Hebrews, is treated here.

paras.t: Impiis autem Ægyptiis usque in novissimum sine misericordia ira supervenit: quia justo judicio permisit eos Omnipotens indurari. Et quamvis ad tempus timore compulsi, aliqualiter pœnituerunt, cito tamen ad pristinam redierunt crudelitatem: sicque ira, id est divina ultio, eis advenit sine misericordia, quia de pœna temporali, ad æternam prolapsi sunt. Quamvis autem in omni opere atque judicio Dei misericordia sit admixta, in aliquibus tamen dicitur non admixta, quia in eis evidenter ac specialiter prædominatur rigor justitiæ, præsertim in vindictis crudelitatum, quæ directe contrariantur misericordiæ. Unde et Jacobus ait apostolus: Judicium sine misericordia fiet ei, qui non fecerit misericordiam. Hinc in parabola evangelica, de servo nequam qui conservo suo noluit misereri, asseritur, quod dominus debita ei dimissa ab eo repetiit, atque in carcerem misit eum quousque debitum solveret universum. Præsciebat enim et futura illorum, id est, Deus præcognovit futuram Ægyptiorum vitiositatem: ideo juste deseruit eos, quia jam ante similia egerant mala.
paras.en: [[19:1|But as to the wicked|Impiis autem]] Egyptians, [[19:1|even to the end there came upon them wrath without mercy|usque in novissimum sine misericordia ira supervenit]]: for by a just judgment the Almighty permitted them to be hardened. And although for a time, driven by fear, they repented after a fashion, they soon went back to their former cruelty: and so wrath, that is, divine vengeance, came upon them without mercy, for from temporal punishment they fell into eternal. Now although mercy is mingled in every work and judgment of God, yet in some it is said not to be mingled, because in them the rigour of justice plainly and especially prevails, above all in the punishment of cruelties, which are directly contrary to mercy. Hence the apostle James also says: [[Jas 2:13|judgment without mercy to him that hath not done mercy|Judicium sine misericordia fiet ei, qui non fecerit misericordiam]]. Hence in the gospel parable of the wicked servant who would not have pity on his fellow servant, it is said that the lord demanded back from him the debts he had forgiven him, and sent him to prison until he should pay the whole debt[[Matt 18:34||]]. [[19:1|For he knew before also what they would do|Præsciebat enim et futura illorum]]: that is, God foreknew the future wickedness of the Egyptians; therefore he justly forsook them, for they had already done like evils before.

paras.t: Quoniam quum ipsi reversi essent, id est, quum Ægyptii a sua ferocitate in Hebræos cessassent ad modicum tempus, et permisissent ut se educerent, id est, ut filii Israel se ipsos de terra Ægypti educerent, et cum magna sollicitudine præmisissent illos, id est, filios Israel sollicite misissent ante se ad exeundum: nam cogebant eos exire velociter; consequebatur illos, puta Ægyptios, pœnitentiæ actus, id est actualis mœror seu pœnitudo de hoc, quod permiserant filios Israel egredi, dicentes: Quid volumus facere, ut dimitteremus Israel, ne serviret nobis?
paras.en: [[19:2|For when|Quoniam quum]] they had turned back [Denis's text reads *reversi essent*, "had turned back", which the Vulgate does not have], that is, when the Egyptians had ceased for a short time from their ferocity against the Hebrews, [[19:2|they had given them leave to depart|permisissent ut se educerent]], that is, leave for the children of Israel to lead themselves out of the land of Egypt, [[19:2|and had sent them away with great care|et cum magna sollicitudine præmisissent illos]], that is, had anxiously sent the children of Israel on ahead of them to go out: for they pressed them to go out speedily[[Ex 12:33||]] [the margin gives Exod. xii, 13; the verse meant is Ex 12:33]; [[19:2|they repented|pœnitentiæ actus]] [Denis's text reads *consequebatur illos pœnitentiæ actus*, "an act of repentance followed them", namely the Egyptians; the Vulgate has *consequebantur illos, pœnitentia acti*, "moved by repentance, they pursued them"]: that is, actual grief or regret that they had let the children of Israel go out, saying: [[Ex 14:5|What meant we to do, that we let Israel go from serving us?|Quid volumus facere, ut dimitteremus Israel, ne serviret nobis?]]

paras.t: Adhuc enim inter manus habentes luctum de morte primogenitorum suorum, et deplorantes eos ad monumenta mortuorum, aliam sibi assumpserunt cogitationem inscientiæ, id est cogitationem stultam et fatuam, ut scilicet filios Israel violenter reducerent. Unde legitur: Immutatum est cor Pharaonis et servorum ejus super populo, et persecuti sunt filios Israel. Et quos rogantes projecerant: nam Pharao dixit, Abeuntes benedicite mihi; hos tanquam fugitivos persequebantur.
paras.en: [[19:3|For whilst they were yet mourning|Adhuc enim inter manus habentes luctum]] for the death of their firstborn, [[19:3|and lamenting at the graves of the dead|et deplorantes eos ad monumenta mortuorum]], [[19:3|they took up another foolish device|aliam sibi assumpserunt cogitationem inscientiæ]], that is, a stupid and senseless design, namely to bring back the children of Israel by force. Hence we read: [[Ex 14:5|the heart of Pharao and of his servants was changed with regard to the people|Immutatum est cor Pharaonis et servorum ejus super populo]], and [[Ex 14:8|he pursued the children of Israel|persecuti sunt filios Israel]] [Denis has "they pursued"]. And those [[19:3|whom they had pressed to be gone|Et quos rogantes projecerant]] (for Pharao said: [[Ex 12:32|departing bless me|Abeuntes benedicite mihi]]), these they [[19:3|pursued them as fugitives|hos tanquam fugitivos persequebantur]].

paras.t: Ducebat enim illos, puta Ægyptios, ad hunc finem, id est ad finalem Hebræorum persecutionem, et ad tam consummatam impietatem ac obstinationem, digna necessitas, id est justum judicium Dei, hoc est derelictio qua eos sic excæcari permisit, et quia volebat eos digne punire maris Rubri submersione. Juxta quem sensum Propheta dixit ad regem Israel: Scio quia cogitavit Dominus interficere te, quia non acquievisti consilio meo. Et horum quæ acciderant, commemorationem amittebant: id est, non attendebant, nec recolebant quoties et quam dire fuerunt plagati a Deo, eo quod nollent Hebræos dimittere, quatenus ex hac consideratione metuerent rursus plagari, si illos persequerentur: et hæc fuit mira excæcatio. Ut quæ deerant tormentis eis jam ante inflictis, repleret punitio, id est, demersio eorum in mari Rubro suppleret. Et quod ait, Ut, tenetur hic concomitanter, non causaliter, quantum ad Ægyptiorum intentionem. Sed quoad divinæ providentiæ dispositionem, tenetur causaliter: quia ob hoc Deus permisit eos tam mirabiliter et quasi tam incredibiliter obtenebrari, nec tot et tantis vexationibus erudiri, ut plenam acciperent punitionem per submersionem.
paras.en: For [[19:4|brought them|Ducebat enim illos]], namely the Egyptians, [[19:4|to this end|ad hunc finem]], that is, to the final persecution of the Hebrews and to so complete an impiety and obstinacy, [[19:4|a necessity, of which they were worthy|digna necessitas]]: that is, the just judgment of God, namely the forsaking by which he permitted them to be so blinded, and because he willed to punish them as they deserved by drowning in the Red Sea. In this sense the Prophet said to the king of Israel: [[2 Par 25:16|I know that God is minded to kill thee|Scio quia cogitavit Dominus interficere te]], because thou [[2 Par 25:16|hast not hearkened to my counsel|non acquievisti consilio meo]] [the margin gives I Par. xxv, 6; the passage is 2 Par 25:16, where the prophet speaks to Amasias, king of Juda]. [[19:4|and they lost the remembrance of those things which had happened|Et horum quæ acciderant, commemorationem amittebant]]: that is, they did not heed or call to mind how often and how terribly they had been struck by God because they would not let the Hebrews go, so that from this consideration they might fear to be struck again if they pursued them: and this was a marvellous blindness. [[19:4|that their punishment might fill up what was wanting to their torments|ut quæ deerant tormentis repleret punitio]] already inflicted on them: that is, that their drowning in the Red Sea might make it up. And when he says *that*, it is taken here as concomitant, not causal, as regards the intention of the Egyptians [that is, it states what followed, not what they meant]. But as regards the ordering of divine providence it is taken as causal: for God permitted them to be darkened so marvellously and almost so incredibly, and not to be taught by so many and so great afflictions, for this end, that they might receive full punishment by drowning.

paras.t: Et populus quidem tuus mirabiliter transiret per fundum maris Rubri divisi; illi autem novam mortem invenirent in sua submersione: quod genus mortis ante non fuit, ut scilicet aliquis exercitus ita tentaret transire per fundum aquæ, hinc inde instar muri stantis in sua divisione, et relabentibus aquis ad locum priorem, ipsis fluctibus involveretur. Vel dicitur, nova mors, respectu occisionis primogenitorum, quæ paulo ante præcessit.
paras.en: [[19:5|And that thy people might wonderfully pass through|Et populus quidem tuus mirabiliter transiret]] across the bottom of the Red Sea divided [Denis's text adds *per fundum maris Rubri divisi*]; [[19:5|but they might find a new death|illi autem novam mortem invenirent]] in their drowning: a kind of death that had not been before, namely that an army should so attempt to pass across the bottom of the water, which stood on either side like a wall where it was divided[[Ex 14:22||]], and, the waters falling back to their former place, should be rolled up in the very waves[[Ex 14:27||]]. Or it is called a new death in respect of the slaying of the firstborn, which had gone a little before.

paras.t: Omnis enim creatura ad suum genus, id est ad generationis suæ originem, seu ad suum generatorem, ab initio refigurabatur, id est, transmutabatur, obediendo Creatoris imperio, per obedientialem potentiam. Ideo sequitur, deserviens tuis præceptis, ut pueri tui, scilicet filii Israel, custodirentur illæsi.
paras.en: [[19:6|For every creature, according to its kind|Omnis enim creatura ad suum genus]], that is, according to the origin of its generation, or to its begetter, [[19:6|was fashioned again as from the beginning|ab initio refigurabatur]], that is, was changed, obeying the command of the Creator by obediential power [that is, the capacity of every creature to be acted on by God beyond its natural powers]. Therefore there follows: [[19:6|obeying thy commandments|deserviens tuis præceptis]], [[19:6|that thy children|ut pueri tui]], namely the children of Israel, [[19:6|might be kept without hurt|custodirentur illæsi]].
