paras.t: Nam nubes eorum castra, id est tentoria et phalangas, obumbrabat contra solis ardorem; vel, Obumbrabat, id est protegebat, ita quod Ægyptii insequentes non valebant tota nocte Hebræos accedere, juxta illud: Tollens se angelus Dei, qui præcedebat castra Israel, abiit post eos, et cum eo pariter columna nubis, inter castra Ægyptiorum et castra Israel: ita ut ad se invicem toto noctis tempore accedere non valerent. Et ex aqua quæ ante erat, id est, paulo ante operuit fundum maris Rubri, terra arida apparuit, id est, fundus ille fuit miraculose siccatus, facta aquæ divisione; et in mari Rubro via sine impedimento, id est, via expedita parata est eis in fundo maris illius, ipso mari diviso, et in sua soliditate stante ex parte utraque; et campus germinans de profundo nimio, id est, ipse fundus præfatus tanquam germinans campus, stetit discoopertus et pulcher; per quem omnis natio transivit, quæ tegebatur tua manu, id est totus populus Israel tua potestate protectus, quæ non permisit aquas divisas cadere super eos, videntes ipsi filii Israel tua mirabilia et monstra, id est signa et miracula tua, monstratione dignissima, videlicet maris Rubri divisionem, et aquarum ejus consolidationem, et qualiter angelus posuit nubem inter eos atque Ægyptios.
paras.en: [[19:7|For a cloud|Nam nubes]] [[19:7|overshadowed|obumbrabat]] [[19:7|their camps|eorum castra]], that is, their tents and companies, against the heat of the sun; or, *overshadowed*, that is, protected, so that the Egyptians in pursuit could not come at the Hebrews all the night, according to that text: [[Ex 14:19|the angel of God, who went before the camp of Israel, removing, went behind them: and together with him the pillar of the cloud|Tollens se angelus Dei, qui præcedebat castra Israel, abiit post eos, et cum eo pariter columna nubis]], [[Ex 14:20|between the Egyptians' camp and the camp of Israel|inter castra Ægyptiorum et castra Israel]]: [[Ex 14:20|so that they could not come at one another all the night|ita ut ad se invicem toto noctis tempore accedere non valerent]]. [[19:7|and where water was before|Et ex aqua quæ ante erat]], that is, which a little before covered the bottom of the Red Sea, [[19:7|dry land appeared|terra arida apparuit]]: that is, that bottom was miraculously dried when the water was divided; [[19:7|and in the Red Sea a way without hindrance|et in mari Rubro via sine impedimento]]: that is, a clear way was made ready for them on the bottom of that sea, the sea itself being divided and standing firm on either side; [[19:7|and out of the great deep a springing field|et campus germinans de profundo nimio]]: that is, that bottom stood uncovered and fair like a field in bloom; [[19:8|Through which all the nation passed|per quem omnis natio transivit]], [[19:8|which was protected with thy hand|quæ tegebatur tua manu]], that is, the whole people of Israel protected by thy power, which did not let the divided waters fall upon them, the children of Israel themselves [[19:8|seeing|videntes]] [[19:8|thy miracles and wonders|tua mirabilia et monstra]], that is, thy signs and miracles, most worthy to be shown [Denis plays on *monstra*, "wonders", and *monstratio*, "showing"]: namely the dividing of the Red Sea, the making firm of its waters, and how the angel set the cloud between them and the Egyptians.

paras.t: Tanquam equi enim depaverunt escam, id est, pastum receperunt de spoliis Ægyptiorum: quos e mari projectos super littus, nudaverunt armis et rebus aliis pretiosis, secundum Hebræos, ut tactum est supra. Et tanquam agni exsultaverunt de sua liberatione: juxta illud in Psalmo, Montes exsultaverunt ut arietes, et colles sicut agni ovium; magnificantes, id est, magnum, pium, justum, omnipotentem confitentes, te, Domine, qui liberasti illos. Unde legitur in Propheta: Qui scidit aquas ante eos: qui duxit eos per abyssos, quasi equum in deserto non impingentem, quasi animal in campo descendens, ut faceret sibi nomen sempiternum.
paras.en: [[19:9|For they fed on their food like horses|Tanquam equi enim depaverunt escam]]: that is, they took their fodder from the spoils of the Egyptians, whom, when they were cast out of the sea upon the shore, they stripped of their arms and other precious things, according to the Hebrews, as was touched on above[[Wis 10:19||]]. [[19:9|and they skipped like lambs|Et tanquam agni exsultaverunt]] for their deliverance, according to that in the Psalm: [[Ps 113:4|The mountains skipped like rams, and the hills like the lambs of the flock.|Montes exsultaverunt ut arietes, et colles sicut agni ovium]]; [[19:9|praising|magnificantes]], that is, confessing as great, loving, just and almighty, [[19:9|thee, O Lord, who hadst delivered them|te, Domine, qui liberasti illos]]. Hence we read in the Prophet: [[Is 63:12|that divided the waters before them|Qui scidit aquas ante eos]]: [[Is 63:13|He that led them out through the deep, as a horse in the wilderness that stumbleth not|qui duxit eos per abyssos, quasi equum in deserto non impingentem]], [[Is 63:14|As a beast that goeth down in the field|quasi animal in campo descendens]], [[Is 63:12|to make himself an everlasting name|ut faceret sibi nomen sempiternum]] [Denis gives the last words of Is 63:12 at the end].

paras.t: Memores enim adhuc erant, post egressum de mari Rubro, eorum quæ in incolatu illorum facta fuerunt mirabilium, quæ Deus fecit pro eis contra Ægyptios, quando ipsi adhuc in Ægypto manebant; quemadmodum pro natione animalium produxit terra muscas, id est, pro generatione utilium bestiarum eruperunt de terra Ægypti innumerabiles muscæ, quæ pungebant Ægyptios. Unde Dominus ait: Ecce ego mittam in te, et in populum tuum, omne genus muscarum. Et pro piscibus eructavit, id est emisit, fluvius Nili, imo diversi fluvii in Ægypto, multitudinem ranarum, quæ operuerunt et impleverunt terram, domos, cubilia, lectos, et cibos Ægyptiorum, ut Exodus narrat.
paras.en: [[19:10|For they were yet mindful|Memores enim adhuc erant]], after coming out of the Red Sea, [[19:10|of those things which had been done in the time of their sojourning|eorum quæ in incolatu illorum facta fuerunt]], the wonders [Denis's text adds *mirabilium*] which God did for them against the Egyptians while they still dwelt in Egypt: [[19:10|how the ground brought forth flies instead of cattle|quemadmodum pro natione animalium produxit terra muscas]], that is, instead of a brood of useful beasts there burst forth from the land of Egypt countless flies, which stung the Egyptians. Hence the Lord says: [[Ex 8:21|behold I will send in upon thee|Ecce ego mittam in te]], and upon thy people, [[Ex 8:21|all kind of flies|omne genus muscarum]]. And [[19:10|instead of fishes|Et pro piscibus]] [[19:10|the river|fluvius]] Nile, or rather the various rivers of Egypt, [[19:10|cast up|eructavit]], that is, sent forth, [[19:10|a multitude of frogs|multitudinem ranarum]], which covered and filled the land[[Ex 8:6||]], the houses, the bedchambers, the beds and the food of the Egyptians[[Ex 8:3||]], as Exodus relates [the margin gives Exod. v, 6, 3; the verses meant are Ex 8:6 and 8:3].

paras.t: Novissime autem, id est post prædicta, scilicet in deserto, viderunt novam creaturam avium, id est, filii Israel conspexerunt copiosissimam coturnicum multitudinem sibi advenientem, ut dictum est supra. Eadem autem sententia in isto libro frequenter sub aliis verbis repetitur: quibus non congruit immorari. Quum abducti concupiscentia, id est, per concupiscentiam a recta ratione abstracti ac devii, postulaverunt escas epulationis, dicentes: Quis dabit nobis ad vescendum carnes? ut legitur in Numeris.
paras.en: [[19:11|And at length|Novissime autem]], that is, after the things already told, namely in the desert, [[19:11|they saw a new generation of birds|viderunt novam creaturam avium]]: that is, the children of Israel beheld a most plentiful multitude of quails coming to them, as was said above[[Wis 16:2||]]. Now the same thought is often repeated in this book in other words, on which it is not fitting to dwell. [[19:11|when being led by their appetite|Quum abducti concupiscentia]], that is, drawn away and gone astray from right reason through concupiscence, [[19:11|they asked for delicate meats|postulaverunt escas epulationis]], saying: [[Num 11:4|Who shall give us flesh to eat?|Quis dabit nobis ad vescendum carnes?]], as we read in Numbers.

paras.t: In allocutione enim desiderii, id est ad petitionem qua appetitum suum de esu carnium petierunt impleri, ascendit illis de mari ortygometra, id est coturnix, juxta illud in Psalmo: Petierunt, et venit coturnix. Quæ venit eis ab insula nomine Ortygia, et volavit per mare usque ad eos. Et vexationes peccatoribus supervenerunt. Posset hoc exponi de prætactis filiis Israel, qui una cum vulgo promiscuo, quod cum eis venerat ex Ægypto, propter inordinatam suam concupiscentiam sunt percussi. Sed verba sequentia pandunt hæc de Ægyptiis dici: quibus in Ægypto ante egressum filiorum Israel supervenerunt multarum atque magnarum vexationes plagarum. Non sine illis, id est simul cum illis, quæ ante facta erant argumentis per vim fluminum, id est cum punitionibus et correptionibus, quas sustinuerunt ex hoc, quod flumina erant in sanguinem versa, piscesque mortui, et computruit fluvius, ita quod defuit aqua Ægyptiis ad potandum. Postea quoque fluvii ranas eructaverunt.
paras.en: [[19:12|For to satisfy their desire|In allocutione enim desiderii]], that is, at the request by which they asked to have their appetite for eating flesh fulfilled, [[19:12|the quail came up to them from the sea|ascendit illis de mari ortygometra]], that is, the quail, according to that in the Psalm: [[Ps 104:40|They asked, and the quail came|Petierunt, et venit coturnix]]. It came to them from an island named Ortygia and flew across the sea to them[[Num 11:31||]]. [[19:12|and punishments came upon the sinners|Et vexationes peccatoribus supervenerunt]]. This could be explained of the children of Israel just mentioned, who, together with the mixed multitude that had come with them out of Egypt[[Ex 12:38||]], were struck for their disordered concupiscence[[Num 11:33||]]. But the words that follow show that this is said of the Egyptians, upon whom, in Egypt, before the children of Israel went out, there came the afflictions of many and great plagues. [[19:12|not without|Non sine illis]], that is, together with, [[19:12|foregoing signs by the force of thunders|quæ ante facta erant argumentis per vim fluminum]] [Denis reads *fluminum*, "of rivers", where the Vulgate has *fulminum*, "of thunders"]: that is, with the punishments and chastisements which they suffered because the rivers were turned into blood[[Ex 7:20||]], and the fish died, and the river grew foul[[Ex 7:21||]], so that the Egyptians had no water to drink[[Ex 7:24||]]. Afterwards too the rivers belched forth frogs[[Ex 8:3||]] [the margin gives Exod. viii with the verse unread; Ex 8:3 or 8:6].

paras.t: Juste enim patiebantur secundum suas nequitias. Etenim detestabiliorem, id est valde detestabilem, seu aliis vitiis graviorem, inhospitalitatem instituerunt Ægyptii, quum tamen hospitalitas virtus sit ad misericordiam pertinens: et ita fuerunt inhumani atque crudeles. Alii quidem, id est quidam Ægyptiorum, ignotos non recipiebant advenas ad hospitandum vel commorandum; alii autem bonos hospites, scilicet filios Israel inter se commorantes, in servitutem redigebant, post mortem Joseph, quum multiplicati fuissent ibidem, ut in Exodo dicitur.
paras.en: [[19:12|for they suffered justly according to their own wickedness|Juste enim patiebantur secundum suas nequitias]]. [[19:13|For they exercised a more detestable|Etenim detestabiliorem]], that is, a very detestable one, or one graver than other vices, [[19:13|inhospitality|inhospitalitatem instituerunt]], namely the Egyptians, although hospitality is a virtue belonging to mercy: and so they were inhuman and cruel. [[19:13|others indeed|Alii quidem]], that is, some of the Egyptians, [[19:13|received not strangers unknown to them|ignotos non recipiebant advenas]] to lodge or to dwell with them; [[19:13|but these brought their guests into bondage that had deserved well of them|alii autem bonos hospites in servitutem redigebant]], the good guests being the children of Israel who dwelt among them; this was after the death of Joseph, when they had multiplied there[[Ex 1:7||]], as is said in Exodus [the margin gives Exod. i with the verse unread; Ex 1:6–7, and the bondage in vv. 8–14].

paras.t: Et non solum hoc malum fecerunt Ægyptii, sed et alius quidem respectus erat illorum, id est alia vitiosa intentio seu consideratio: quoniam inviti, id est cum duritia et abominatione, recipiebant extraneos.
paras.en: [[19:14|And not only so|Et non solum]] did the Egyptians do this evil, [[19:14|but in another respect|sed et alius quidem respectus erat illorum]], that is, another wicked intention or regard: [[19:14|for the others against their will|quoniam inviti]], that is, with harshness and loathing, [[19:14|received the strangers|recipiebant extraneos]].

paras.t: Qui autem cum lætitia receperunt hos, qui eisdem usi erant institutis, id est, Ægyptii usi prætactis crudelibus institutis, hos qui cum lætitia receperunt, id est filios Israel, qui benigne et jucunde receperunt extraneos ad hospitium aut cohabitationem, sævissimis afflixerunt doloribus, perducentes vitam Hebræorum ad amaritudinem magnam. Sicque Ægyptii prohibuerunt filios Israel a pia extraneorum susceptione.
paras.en: [[19:15|them whom they had received with joy|Qui autem cum lætitia receperunt hos]], [[19:15|who lived under the same laws|qui eisdem usi erant institutis]] [Denis reads *institutis*, "customs", for the Vulgate's *justitiis*, and takes the verse thus: the Egyptians, who followed those customs, afflicted the Israelites, who received strangers with joy]: that is, the Egyptians, who followed the cruel customs already mentioned, [[19:15|grievously afflicted|sævissimis afflixerunt doloribus]] those who received with joy, that is, the children of Israel, who kindly and gladly received strangers to lodge or dwell with them, bringing the life of the Hebrews to great bitterness. And so the Egyptians kept the children of Israel from the godly welcoming of strangers.

paras.t: Percussi sunt autem Ægyptii cæcitate interiori incorrigibilis incredulitatis ac vitiorum, cæcitate quoque exteriori, id est, luminis intuitione [caruerunt] in triduo palpabilium tenebrarum: et hoc, propter prætacta eorum facinora. Quemadmodum enim beati misericordes, quoniam ipsi misericordiam consequentur; sic infelices sunt immisericordes, quoniam donis gratiæ et gloriæ privabuntur. Sicut illi in foribus justi Lot, id est, sicut Sodomitæ fuerunt percussi quadam specie cæcitatis: quæ species acrisia nuncupatur, qua aliquid confuse conspicitur, non tamen discernere potest adspiciens, quis aut quid sit illud. De qua re in Genesi scriptum est. Denique justitiæ Lot attestatur princeps Apostolorum in secunda sua Canonica: Adspectu, inquiens, et auditu justus erat, habitans apud eos qui de die in diem animam justam iniquis operibus cruciabant. Quum subitaneis cooperti essent tenebris Ægyptii in triduo memorato, unusquisque transitum ostii sui quærebat, id est, invenire optabat, vel ad intrandum, si forte extra fuit, vel ad egrediendum, si fuerat intus, quum tamen se non possent de locis suis movere. Vel intelligitur de Sodomitis, qui præfatæ cæcitatis caligine cæsi, januam quam quærebant, invenire nequibant.
paras.en: [[19:16|But they were struck with blindness|Percussi sunt autem Ægyptii cæcitate]], the Egyptians, with the inner blindness of incorrigible unbelief and of vices, and also with outward blindness: that is, they were deprived of the sight of light in the three days of darkness that could be felt[[Ex 10:21||]][[Ex 10:22||]]; and this for their crimes already mentioned. For as [[Matt 5:7|Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy|beati misericordes, quoniam ipsi misericordiam consequentur]], so the unmerciful are unhappy, for they will be deprived of the gifts of grace and glory. [[19:16|as those others were at the doors of the just man|Sicut illi in foribus justi]], Lot: that is, as the Sodomites were struck with a certain kind of blindness, the kind called *acrisia* [Greek, "indiscernment"], by which a thing is seen confusedly, yet the one looking cannot tell who or what it is. Of this it is written in Genesis[[Gen 19:11||]]. And the prince of the Apostles bears witness to Lot's justice in his second canonical epistle, saying: [[2 Pet 2:8|in sight|Adspectu]], he says, [[2 Pet 2:8|and hearing he was just, dwelling among them who from day to day vexed the just soul with unjust works|et auditu justus erat, habitans apud eos qui de die in diem animam justam iniquis operibus cruciabant]]. [[19:16|when they were covered with sudden darkness|Quum subitaneis cooperti essent tenebris]], the Egyptians, in the three days mentioned, [[19:16|and every one sought the passage of his own door|unusquisque transitum ostii sui quærebat]]: that is, longed to find it, either to go in, if perhaps he was outside, or to go out, if he was inside, though they could not move from their places[[Ex 10:23||]]. Or it is understood of the Sodomites, who, struck by the mist of the blindness just described, could not find the door they were seeking.

paras.t: In se enim elementa dum convertuntur, id est, dum mutuo contemperantur et alterantur, mutando naturalem modum agendi, sicut in organo, id est musico instrumento, qualitatis sonus immutatur: quoniam sonus ille nunc intentior, nunc remissior est, secundum quod ludens in hujusmodi instrumento, diversimode tangit chordas: quarum tamen soni diversi in unam consonantiam redigantur; et omnia suum sonum custodiunt, id est, proprium sonitum habent ac reddunt, juxta voluntatem modulantis in organo: ita, supple, elementa, diversimode alterantur et contemperantur, ac diversimode agunt, secundum Creatoris imperium, qui cuncta instituit ut suæ obediant jussioni. Unde æstimari ex ipso visu certo potest: id est, per experientiam et visus evidentiam patet hoc verum esse.
paras.en: [[19:17|For while the elements are changed in themselves|In se enim elementa dum convertuntur]], that is, while they temper and alter one another, changing their natural manner of acting, [[19:17|as in an instrument|sicut in organo]], that is, a musical instrument, [[19:17|the sound of the quality is changed|qualitatis sonus immutatur]]: for that sound is now higher, now lower, according as the player of such an instrument touches the strings in different ways, whose different sounds are nevertheless brought into one harmony; [[19:17|yet all keep their sound|et omnia suum sonum custodiunt]], that is, they have and give their own sound, according to the will of the one playing on the instrument: so (supply) the elements are altered and tempered in different ways, and act in different ways, according to the command of the Creator, who made all things to obey his bidding. [[19:17|which may clearly be perceived by the very sight|Unde æstimari ex ipso visu certo potest]]: that is, by experience and by the evidence of sight it is plain that this is true.

paras.t: Agrestia enim in aquatica convertebantur: id est, animalia quorum natura est super terram deambulare, modum et proprietatem piscium assumpserunt, eundo per fundum Rubri maris, in quo pisces solent natare; et quæcumque erant natantia, sicut ranæ, quæ morantur et natant in aquis, in terra transibant: quia exeuntes de fluviis, venerunt per siccam terram ad domos Ægyptiorum. Hebræi autem greges pecorum suorum secum duxerunt per maris Rubri profundum, juxta illud: Cuncti greges pergent nobiscum.
paras.en: [[19:18|For the things of the land were turned into things of the water|Agrestia enim in aquatica convertebantur]]: that is, animals whose nature is to walk upon the earth took on the manner and property of fishes, going across the bottom of the Red Sea, in which fishes are wont to swim; [[19:18|and the things that before swam in the water|et quæcumque erant natantia]], such as frogs, which live and swim in the waters, [[19:18|passed upon the land|in terra transibant]]: for coming out of the rivers[[Ex 8:6||]], they came across the dry land to the houses of the Egyptians[[Ex 8:3||]]. And the Hebrews led the flocks of their cattle with them across the depth of the Red Sea, according to that text: [[Ex 10:26|All the flocks shall go with us|Cuncti greges pergent nobiscum]].

paras.t: Ignis in aqua valebat supra suam virtutem, id est, ultra solitum intentioris fuit caloris: quando videlicet, ut in Exodo narratur, ignis et grando, nix et aqua pariter descenderunt super Ægyptios, ut supra expositum est; et aqua exstinguentis naturæ obliviscebatur, id est, per modum obliviscentis se habuit, non exstinguendo ignem, secum tunc descendentem.
paras.en: [[19:19|The fire had power in water above its own virtue|Ignis in aqua valebat supra suam virtutem]], that is, it was of more intense heat than usual: namely when, as is related in Exodus, fire and hail, snow and water came down together upon the Egyptians, as was explained above; [[19:19|and the water forgot its quenching nature|et aqua exstinguentis naturæ obliviscebatur]], that is, it behaved as one forgetting itself, not quenching the fire that then came down with it.

paras.t: Flammæ econtrario corruptibilium animalium, utpote serpentium diversi generis, et draconum, igneas flammas spirantium, non vexaverunt carnes coambulantium, id est, non læserunt corpora Hebræorum, nec jumenta ipsorum ambulantium per desertum, in quo erant hujusmodi animalia venenosa ignita. Hinc habetur in Deuteronomio: Dominus ductor tuus fuit in solitudine magna atque terribili, in qua erat serpens flatu adurens, et scorpio, ac dipsas. Et constat quod venenosa illa, nec filiis Israel, nec eorum pecoribus nocuerunt, nisi quod interdum propter peccata sua puniebantur. Nec dissolvebant illam quæ facile dissolvebatur, sicut glacies, bonam escam, id est, non liquefaciebant ipsum manna, quod faciliter liquefiebat radio solis, sicut glacies calore ignis ac solis cito dissolvitur.
paras.en: [[19:20|On the other side, the flames|Flammæ econtrario]] [[19:20|of corruptible animals|corruptibilium animalium]], such as serpents of divers kinds and dragons, breathing fiery flames, [[19:20|wasted not the flesh|non vexaverunt carnes]] of those [[19:20|walking therein|coambulantium]] [Denis takes *corruptibilium animalium* with *flammæ*, "the flames of corruptible animals", and *coambulantium* as "of those walking together"]: that is, they did not harm the bodies of the Hebrews, nor their beasts, as they walked through the desert, in which there were such venomous fiery animals. Hence we have in Deuteronomy: The Lord [[Deut 8:15|was thy leader in the great and terrible wilderness, wherein there was the serpent burning with his breath, and the scorpion and the dipsas|ductor tuus fuit in solitudine magna atque terribili, in qua erat serpens flatu adurens, et scorpio, ac dipsas]]. And it is certain that those venomous creatures did harm neither to the children of Israel nor to their cattle, except that at times they were punished for their sins. [[19:20|neither did they melt|Nec dissolvebant illam]] that [[19:20|which was apt to melt as ice|quæ facile dissolvebatur, sicut glacies]], [[19:20|that good food|bonam escam]]: that is, they did not melt the manna itself, which melted easily in the ray of the sun[[Ex 16:21||]], as ice quickly melts by the heat of fire and of the sun.

paras.t: In omnibus enim magnificasti populum tuum, Domine: id est, populum Israel in multis et magnis beneficiis spiritualibus et corporalibus eminentem fecisti præ ceteris gentibus; et honorasti, id est, honorabilem constituisti, et non despexisti preces eorum, in omni tempore, et in omni loco, scilicet in Ægypto, in mari Rubro, in deserto, in Jordane, in terra promissionis, adsistens eis per gratiam specialem, præsertim electis ex eis: reprobos autem et ingratos damnasti. Hinc in Deuteronomio Moyses huic populo ait: Quæ est alia gens sic inclyta, ut habeat cærimonias, justaque judicia, et universam legem quam ego proponam hodie ante oculos vestros? Et rursus: Interroga de diebus antiquis, qui fuerunt ante te, ex die qua creavit Deus hominem super terram, a summo cœli usque ad summum ejus: si facta est aliquando hujusmodi res, aut unquam cognitum est, ut audiret populus vocem Dei loquentis de medio ignis, sicut tu audisti, vixisti et vidisti; si fecit Deus ut ingrederetur, et tolleret sibi gentem de medio nationum, per tentationes, signa atque portenta, per pugnam et robustam manum, extentumque brachium, et horribiles visiones, juxta omnia quæ fecit pro vobis in Ægypto Dominus Deus vester, videntibus oculis tuis: ut scires quoniam Dominus ipse est Deus, et non est alius præter unum.
paras.en: [[19:20|For in all things thou didst magnify thy people, O Lord|In omnibus enim magnificasti populum tuum, Domine]]: that is, thou didst make the people of Israel eminent above other nations in many and great benefits, spiritual and bodily; [[19:20|and didst honour them|et honorasti]], that is, didst make them honourable, [[19:20|and didst not despise|et non despexisti]] their prayers, [[19:20|at all times, and in every place|in omni tempore, et in omni loco]], namely in Egypt, in the Red Sea, in the desert, at the Jordan, in the land of promise, [[19:20|but didst assist them|adsistens eis]] by special grace, above all the elect among them; but the reprobate and ungrateful thou didst condemn. Hence in Deuteronomy Moses says to this people: [[Deut 4:8|what other nation is there so renowned that hath ceremonies, and just judgments, and all the law, which I will set forth this day before our eyes?|Quæ est alia gens sic inclyta, ut habeat cærimonias, justaque judicia, et universam legem quam ego proponam hodie ante oculos vestros?]] And again: [[Deut 4:32|Ask of the days of old, that have been before thy time from the day that God created man upon the earth, from one end of heaven to the other end thereof, if ever there was done the like thing, or it hath been known at any time|Interroga de diebus antiquis, qui fuerunt ante te, ex die qua creavit Deus hominem super terram, a summo cœli usque ad summum ejus: si facta est aliquando hujusmodi res, aut unquam cognitum est]], [[Deut 4:33|That a people should hear the voice of God speaking out of the midst of fire, as thou hast heard, and lived|ut audiret populus vocem Dei loquentis de medio ignis, sicut tu audisti, vixisti]], and seen; [[Deut 4:34|If God ever did so as to go, and take to himself a nation out of the midst of nations by temptations, signs, and wonders, by fight, and a strong hand, and stretched out arm, and horrible visions according to all the things that the Lord your God did for you in Egypt, before thy eyes|si fecit Deus ut ingrederetur, et tolleret sibi gentem de medio nationum, per tentationes, signa atque portenta, per pugnam et robustam manum, extentumque brachium, et horribiles visiones, juxta omnia quæ fecit pro vobis in Ægypto Dominus Deus vester, videntibus oculis tuis]]: [[Deut 4:35|That thou mightest know that the Lord he is God, and there is no other besides him|ut scires quoniam Dominus ipse est Deus, et non est alius præter unum]].

paras.t: Verum hæc omnia de populo christiano multo sublimius verificantur: spiritualiter tamen, imo et litteraliter pro maxima parte. Cui collata est tanta divinorum plenitudo charismatum, tanta abundantia signorum, virtutum et prodigiorum, tam perfectissima lex, et tanta spiritualium ac corporalium exuberantia beneficiorum, ut quantum veritas præcedit figuram, et umbram lux, tantum populus christianus in omnibus istis populum illum, cui omnia in figura contingebant, excedat. Insuper, quod populus ille olim præ ceteris tam electus, a tempore evangelicæ legis tam extreme relictus est, et cunctis excellentiis suis privatus, dispersus, captivus; atque divina charismata illi olim concessa, ad plebem christianam tam copiosissime et excellentissime sunt translata: certissimum signum est veritatis catholicæ fidei et evangelicæ legis. Ad laudem et gloriam Omnipotentis, qui est super omnia Deus sublimis et benedictus. Amen.
paras.en: But all these things are made true far more sublimely of the Christian people: spiritually, indeed, yet for the most part literally too. On it has been bestowed such fulness of divine gifts, such abundance of signs, powers and wonders, so wholly perfect a law, and such an overflowing of spiritual and bodily benefits, that as far as the truth goes before the figure, and light before the shadow, so far does the Christian people exceed in all these things that people of whom it is written: [[1 Cor 10:11|all these things happened to them in figure|omnia in figura contingebant]]. Moreover, that that people, once so chosen above the rest, has since the time of the gospel law been so utterly forsaken, and deprived of all its excellences, scattered and captive, and that the divine gifts once granted to it have been passed on so most abundantly and most excellently to the Christian people, is a most certain sign of the truth of the Catholic faith and of the gospel law. To the praise and glory of the Almighty, who is God above all, exalted and blessed. Amen.
